definition_zh: 暴怒；狂怒；风行；狂热
definition_en: very strong anger; to speak or act with violent anger; to continue with great force or popularity; a widespread enthusiasm or fashion
core_image: 被砸裂的车门，玻璃上还留着拳印
scene: 停车场里，两名司机为抢一个车位大声争吵，其中一人一拳砸在车门上。 He flew into a rage when another car took the space he had waited for.
sceneCN: 这里 rage 是「暴怒」（第 1 个义项：极其强烈的愤怒）；句意为另一辆车抢走了他等候的车位，他顿时暴怒。画面里可留意：裂开的车门、还留着的拳印、围观的司机。

pos.zh: 狂怒；怒斥；（风暴、时尚）猛烈持续

derivatives.zh: rage 加 -ing，指狂怒的，也指猛烈的，如 raging storm
en- 加 rage，指使某人暴怒

senses.title: Very strong anger
senses.definition: a feeling of violent and uncontrolled anger
senses.definitionCN: 一种猛烈而失控的愤怒
senses.example: He slammed the door in a rage.
senses.exampleCN: 他暴怒之下摔上门。
senses.why: Latin rabies meant madness, and the French word built on it named a fury so strong it looked like madness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rabies 意为疯狂，建立其上的法语词指一种强烈到近乎疯狂的愤怒。

senses.title: To act with violent anger
senses.definition: to speak or behave with violent anger
senses.definitionCN: 带着猛烈怒气说话或行动
senses.example: She raged at the driver for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那名司机怒吼了好几分钟。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, naming the outward behaviour that anger produces rather than the feeling alone.
senses.whyCN: 名词化为动词，指愤怒所产生的外在行为，而不只是感受本身。

senses.title: To continue with great force
senses.definition: to continue violently or spread widely, used of storms, wars and fashions
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈地持续或广泛蔓延，用于风暴、战争与时尚
senses.example: The storm raged all night along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨沿海岸肆虐了一整夜。
senses.why: Anger that cannot be stopped looks like a storm that cannot be stopped, so the word was applied to any force that will not calm.
senses.whyCN: 无法平息的愤怒像无法平息的风暴，于是这个词被用到任何不肯平静的力量上。

senses.title: A widespread fashion
senses.definition: a short period when something is extremely popular
senses.definitionCN: 某事物极受欢迎的短暂时段
senses.example: The new game became a rage among teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新游戏在青少年中风靡一时。
senses.why: A fashion that spreads fast and refuses to be quiet was called a rage, as if enthusiasm were a storm.
senses.whyCN: 一种迅速蔓延、不肯安静的时尚被称作 rage，仿佛热情也是一场风暴。

intro.en: Rage comes through French from the Latin word for madness, and the sense of fury grew from the image of a mind driven out of its normal state.
intro.cn: rage 经法语来自拉丁语表示疯狂的名词，暴怒义从「心智被逐出常态」这一画面生长出来。

items.en: Rabies meant madness or frenzy, and in medicine it also named the disease that causes violent distress.
items.cn: rabies 意为疯狂、狂乱，在医学上也指引起剧烈痛苦的那种疾病。

items.en: The related verb meant to rave or be mad, describing a person beside themselves with feeling.
items.cn: 相关动词意为狂乱、发疯，形容一个人情绪激动到失去常态。

items.en: Old French rage named furious anger and also the violent force of a storm or a disease.
items.cn: 古法语 rage 既指狂怒，也指风暴或疾病的猛烈力量。

items.en: Middle English rage kept both the anger and the storm, so the word could describe a person and a sea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 rage 同时保留了怒气与风暴，所以这个词既能形容人，也能形容海。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a fashion that sweeps a group, as if enthusiasm were weather.
items.cn: 现代英语又增添了「席卷群体的时尚」这一义，仿佛热情也是天气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same word and its Latin relative; the near-meaning group gathers words for anger and frenzy.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的形式及其拉丁亲属；近义组收表示愤怒与狂乱的词。

entries.definition: A viral disease that causes madness in animals.
entries.definitionCN: 使动物发狂的病毒性疾病。

entries.definition: Violent and out of control.
To make someone very angry.
Great anger caused by something unfair, a different formation.
entries.definitionCN: 因不公之事引起的强烈愤慨，构词方式不同。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of displeasure.
Wild and violent anger.
Deep anger, often in a literary or religious tone.
entries.definitionCN: 深重的愤怒，常带文学或宗教语气。

entries.definition: A state of wild uncontrolled activity.

normalIntro.en: The word is madness made social: a feeling, a behaviour, a storm and a fashion all move with the same violence.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把疯狂放进社会：感受、行为、风暴与时尚都以同一种猛烈推进。

normal.en: Rage and rabies share the Latin word for madness, which is why rage feels like something that takes over the body.
normal.cn: rage 与 rabies 共用拉丁语「疯狂」一词，所以暴怒感觉像有东西占据了身体。

normal.en: Fly into a rage is the fixed phrase for anger that arrives suddenly, as if the person were airborne.
normal.cn: fly into a rage 是形容怒气突然降临的固定说法，仿佛人被吹了起来。

normal.en: Road rage names anger that grows inside a car and then escapes through the window.
normal.cn: road rage 指在车里积蓄、再从车窗里泄出的怒气。

normal.en: All the rage means extremely fashionable, as if the fashion were a storm passing through.
normal.cn: all the rage 意为极其时髦，仿佛时尚是一场过境的风暴。

normal.en: A raging storm and a raging man use the same participle, because neither can be calmed quickly.
normal.cn: raging storm 与 raging man 用同一个分词，因为两者都无法迅速平息。

abstract.en: Anger and weather share one word because both are forces people can only wait out.
abstract.cn: 愤怒与天气共用一个词，因为两者都是人们只能等待其过去的力。

abstract.en: A fashion called a rage is a reminder that enthusiasm can behave like a storm and disappear just as fast.
abstract.cn: 被称为 rage 的时尚提醒我们：热情可以像风暴一样出现，也能同样快地消失。

abstract.en: To rage is to insist that the world match your sense of what is right, and the cost is often borne by whoever is nearest.
abstract.cn: 狂怒就是坚持世界必须符合你的是非感，而代价往往由最近的人承担。

examples.en: She was shaking with rage after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，她气得发抖。

examples.en: The storm raged for three days without a pause.
examples.cn: 暴风雨一连肆虐了三天没有停歇。

examples.en: Short jackets were all the rage that spring.
examples.cn: 那个春天短款外套风靡一时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞吉」——怒气像锐利的针扎进来，一下就爆，记住 rage 是暴怒。

root: 拉丁语 rabies（疯狂）→ rabere（发狂）→ 古法语 rage → 英语 rage；同族有 raging、enrage，以及同源的 rabies。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fury near madness; the senses divide into the feeling, its outward action, unstoppable force and a fashion that sweeps through.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「近乎疯狂的暴怒」；义项分为这种感受、它的外在行动、不可阻挡的力量，以及席卷而来的时尚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car door with a fist-shaped dent in the metal.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门上留着一个拳头形状的凹痕。

chain: A STORM THAT WILL NOT STOP

branches.en: a door slammed hard enough to shake
branches.cn: 摔得整扇门都在晃

branches.en: a voice raised at a stranger
branches.cn: 冲着陌生人抬高的嗓音

branches.en: waves hitting a sea wall all night
branches.cn: 整夜拍打海堤的浪

branches.en: a game everyone suddenly plays
branches.cn: 突然人人都在玩的游戏

branches.en: the same violence, once in a person and once in weather
branches.cn: 同一种猛烈，一次在人身上，一次在天气里

intro.en: The word came through French from the Latin noun for madness, and English built its relatives with participles and a prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语表示疯狂的名词，英语用分词与一个前缀构成它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun rabies survives in English as the name of the disease it also described.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 rabies 在英语中存活下来，成为它所描述的那种疾病的名字。

definition_zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；（公众）关注度
definition_en: the distance one can see clearly, or the state of being able to be seen
core_image: 从山脊望向远处，一层层山影越来越淡
scene: 清晨的山路上雾很重，前面的路牌要走近才看得清。 Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 visibility 是「能见度」（第 1 个义项：能看清的距离）；句意为大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。从山脊望出去、远山越来越淡的那幅画面，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；关注度

collocations.phrase: raise the visibility of an issue
collocations.zh: 提高某个议题的关注度

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「可见的；明显的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不可见性」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: The distance one can see
senses.definition: the distance at which objects can be clearly seen, especially in weather reports
senses.definitionCN: 能清晰看见物体的距离，尤用于天气报告
senses.example: Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives vis-, and -ity names a quality, so visibility is literally the quality of being able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出 vis-，-ity 表示性质，所以 visibility 字面上就是「能被看见的程度」。

senses.title: The state of being seen
senses.definition: the fact or degree of something being able to be seen at all
senses.definitionCN: 某物能否被看见、被看见到什么程度
senses.example: The tall trees limited the visibility of the path from the house.
senses.exampleCN: 高树挡住了从屋里看到小路的视线。
senses.why: Strip the weather away and the word still measures how much a thing can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 去掉天气的成分，这个词仍在衡量一件事物能被看到多少。

senses.title: Public attention
senses.definition: the degree to which a person or a cause is noticed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一项事业被公众注意的程度
senses.example: The campaign gave the small charity national visibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动让那家小慈善机构获得全国关注。
senses.why: A cause that can be seen is a cause people can support, so being seen turned into being noticed publicly.
senses.whyCN: 看得见的事业才能得到支持，于是「被看见」变成了「被公众注意」。

senses.title: Clearness of a design or a text
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to see and read, in print or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 印刷或屏幕上易于看见和阅读的程度
senses.example: Contrast improves the visibility of small text on a screen.
senses.exampleCN: 提高对比度可以改善屏幕上小字的清晰度。
senses.why: Typesetters and designers need the same quality as weather forecasters: how well a thing comes to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 排版者与设计师需要的品质和气象预报员一样：东西进入眼睛的效果有多好。

senses.title: The character of being plainly evident
senses.definition: the quality of something being obvious or clear to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对所有人都明显、清楚的性质
senses.example: The visibility of the mistake made the meeting awkward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误太显眼，让会议很尴尬。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be hidden, it is visible in a strong sense, and the noun names that plainness.
senses.whyCN: 若一件事藏不住，它就在强意义上可见，名词便指这种显而易见。

intro.en: Visibility comes from Latin videre, to see, through the adjective visibilis, able to be seen.
intro.cn: visibility 来自拉丁语 videre（看见），经由形容词 visibilis（能被看见的）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and the stem vis- carries that meaning into many English words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，词干 vis- 把这个意思带进许多英语词。

items.en: Visibilis was formed to mean able to be seen.
items.cn: visibilis 构造成「能被看见的」。

items.en: The abstract noun visibilitas named the quality of being seen.
items.cn: 抽象名词 visibilitas 指能被看见这一性质。

items.en: English took visibility in the sixteenth century, mainly in learned writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 visibility，主要用于学术写作。

items.en: Aviation and motoring turned it into a measured distance in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪航空与汽车交通把它变成一个可测的距离。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the words for sight and for being noticed.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收视觉与被注意相关词。

entries.definition: The adjective, meaning able to be seen.
The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
The state of not being able to be seen.
Sight itself, or a picture seen in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 看的能力，或心中所见之景。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen.
The quality of being clear, in air, sound or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 空气、声音或文字清晰的性质。

entries.definition: Public attention given to a person or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 给予人或产品的公众注意。

entries.definition: The state of being important and noticed.

normalIntro.en: The see-root plus -ity: a quality of being seen, measured in metres by pilots and drivers.
normalIntro.cn: 「看」词根加 -ity：一种被看见的性质，又被飞行员与司机用米来量。

normal.en: Vis- means to see, from Latin videre.
normal.cn: vis- 意为看见，源自拉丁语 videre。

normal.en: -ity turns visible into a quality, as in ability and clarity.
normal.cn: -ity 把 visible 变成性质名词，如 ability、clarity。

normal.en: Visibility is uncountable: poor visibility, not a visibility.
normal.cn: visibility 不可数：说 poor visibility。

normal.en: In weather it is a distance; in public life it is attention.
normal.cn: 在天气里它是距离，在公共生活中它是关注。

normal.en: Invisibility is the opposite, formed with in-.
normal.cn: invisibility 是反面，用 in- 构成。

abstract.en: See ridges fading one behind the other into haze.
abstract.cn: 想象一道道山脊越远越淡，没入雾中。

abstract.en: Hear a radio voice giving the distance in metres.
abstract.cn: 听广播报出以米计的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that everyone in the street can read at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块全街人都能同时看清的牌子。

examples.en: Visibility was poor on the mountain road that morning.
examples.cn: 那天早上山路的能见度很差。

examples.en: The new logo increased the brand's visibility.
examples.cn: 新标志提高了品牌的曝光度。

examples.en: Thick glass reduced the visibility of the numbers.
examples.cn: 厚玻璃让数字变得看不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为扎必了体」——雾太浓，为看清路得扎着脖子，能见度实在太低。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（可见的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 visibilitas → 英语 visibility；同根词有 visible、vision、advise。

sensesIntro.en: How well a thing comes to the eye becomes a measured distance, then a share of public attention, then a plainness nobody can miss.
sensesIntro.cn: 「东西进入眼睛的效果」先变成可测的距离，再变成公众关注的一份，最后变成谁都躲不开的显而易见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ridges fading into haze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道道山脊没入雾中。

branches.en: The weather branch: fifty metres on the motorway.
branches.cn: 天气分支：高速路上五十米。

branches.en: The sightline branch: trees blocking the path from the house.
branches.cn: 视线分支：树挡住从屋里看小路的视线。

branches.en: The attention branch: a small charity on national news.
branches.cn: 关注分支：小慈善机构上了全国新闻。

branches.en: The design branch: small text made readable by contrast.
branches.cn: 设计分支：靠对比度让小字可读。

branches.en: The plainness branch: a mistake everyone could see.
branches.cn: 明显分支：人人都看得见的错误。

intro.en: Vis- means to see, -ibilis and -ity make an adjective and then a quality, and in- negates it.
intro.cn: vis- 意为看见，-ibilis 与 -ity 依次造出形容词与性质名词，in- 表示否定。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visibilis are recorded, as is the medieval noun visibilitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visibilis 均有记录，中世纪名词 visibilitas 同样有记录。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: The verb also gives vision and video.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还生出 vision 与 video。

definition_zh: 潜在地；有可能地；从潜力上看
definition_en: in a way that is possible but not yet actual, describing what could happen or what a thing could become
core_image: 一颗包在种皮里的种子，旁边虚线的树影已经画好，但树还没长出来
scene: 这种新菌株可能对每一种药物都具有抗药性。 The new strain is potentially resistant to every drug we have.
sceneCN: 这里 potentially 是「有可能地、潜在地」（第 1 个义项：可能出现但尚未发生）；句意：这种新菌株有可能对我们现有的所有药物都耐药。图中可辨识物件：包着种皮的种子、虚线勾勒的树影、尚未长出的枝条；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 潜在地；有可能地；从潜力上看

senses.title: Possible but not actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在地：可能但还没发生
senses.definition: used to say that something may happen or may be true, without asserting that it does
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事可能发生或可能成立，但不肯定它已经发生或成立
senses.example: The drug is potentially effective, but no trial has been completed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药可能有疗效，但还没有完成试验。
senses.why: potentia in Latin is 'power, capacity'. The adverb marks a capacity that exists before any result, so the statement stays open.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 potentia 是“力量、能力”。这个副词标记先于结果存在的能力，所以陈述保持开放。

senses.title: A latent power
senses.titleCN: 从潜力上看：能力还没释放
senses.definition: with respect to the capacity a person or thing still holds inside and has not yet used
senses.definitionCN: 从人或事物内部尚未释放的能力来看
senses.example: The team is potentially the strongest in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在潜力上是联赛最强的。
senses.why: Here the word measures stored capacity rather than probability. The ranking is about what could be released, not about odds.
senses.whyCN: 这里它衡量的是储存的能力，而非概率。排名评的是可能释放的力量，不是赔率。

senses.title: Risk warning
senses.titleCN: 可能有危害：先提醒再说
senses.definition: used to flag a possible danger while leaving the certainty of that danger unstated
senses.definitionCN: 用于提示可能存在的危险，同时不说明危险的确定程度
senses.example: The chemical is potentially harmful to children.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化学物质可能对儿童有害。
senses.why: Risk language needs a word that names danger without proving it. The adverb lets a warning be urgent and still cautious.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言需要一个既指出危险又不证明危险的词。这个副词让警告既有紧迫感又保持谨慎。

senses.title: Tentative scientific claim
senses.definition: in scientific writing, used to report an inference whose evidence is indirect
senses.definitionCN: 在科学写作中，用于报告证据为间接的推论
senses.example: The pattern is potentially caused by a shift in ocean currents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一模式可能是由洋流变化造成的。
senses.why: Science separates observation from explanation. The adverb marks the step from data to a proposed cause, which is exactly where certainty drops.
senses.whyCN: 科学要把观察与解释分开。这个副词标记从数据迈到所提原因的那一步，而确定性正在这一步下降。

senses.title: Untapped resource
senses.titleCN: 可争取的资源：还没用上
senses.definition: describing a resource, market or worker whose value is available if it is used
senses.definitionCN: 描述资源、市场或劳动者只要被使用就有价值
senses.example: The region is potentially a major market for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区可能成为电动汽车的重要市场。
senses.why: Economics uses the word for value that exists in possibility. The resource is real; only its use is missing.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用它指存在于可能性中的价值。资源是真实的，缺的只是使用。

senses.title: Mathematics and physics
senses.definition: in physics, describing a quantity defined at a point and realized only when something moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中描述某点上的量，只有发生移动或变化时才实现
senses.example: Energy is stored in the field as a potential difference.
senses.exampleCN: 能量以电势差的形式储存在场中。
senses.why: Physics gives the word its most literal sense: potential energy is energy by position, waiting for a release.
senses.whyCN: 物理学给了这个词最字面的义项：势能是按位置拥有的能量，等着被释放。

senses.title: Hedging in argument
senses.definition: used in debate to weaken a claim so that it cannot be refuted too easily
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中用来弱化主张，使其不易被轻易驳倒
senses.example: This approach is potentially more fair, though the data are thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这一做法可能更公平，尽管数据很少。
senses.why: The adverb is a hedge: it transfers the burden of proof from the speaker to future evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是一种模糊限制：把举证责任从说话人转给未来的证据。

senses.title: Possibility in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar teaching, labelling an adverb that expresses possibility rather than certainty
senses.definitionCN: 在语法教学中标记表达可能性而非确定性的副词
senses.example: Potentially is a possibility adverb, like perhaps and conceivably.
senses.exampleCN: potentially 是可能性副词，与“也许”“可以想象地”等词同类。
senses.why: Grammar groups words by what they do to a sentence's certainty. This adverb lowers certainty without cancelling the statement.
senses.whyCN: 语法按“对句子确定性的作用”给词分组。这个副词降低确定性，但不取消陈述。

intro.en: Potentially is potential plus -ly. Potential comes from Latin potentia 'power, ability', from potens 'able, powerful', itself the present participle of posse 'to be able'.
intro.cn: potentially 是 potential 加 -ly。potential 来自拉丁语 potentia“力量、能力”，源于 potens“有能力的”，而 potens 是 posse“能够”的现在分词。

items.en: posse 'to be able' is a contraction of potis esse 'to be able'. potis is an old adjective meaning 'able, capable'.
items.cn: posse“能够”是 potis esse“有能力存在”的缩合。potis 是古形容词，意为“有能力的”。

items.en: The present participle potens 'being able' produced the adjective 'powerful'. From it English takes potent and potency.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens“有能力的”产生形容词“强有力的”。英语由此取得 potent 与 potency。

items.en: potentia abstracted the adjective into a noun: 'power, capacity, force'. The noun could mean capacity in the sense of what a thing can become.
items.cn: potentia 把形容词抽象为名词：力量、能力、势力。该名词也可指事物可能成为的那种“能力”。

items.en: English forms potential in the 14th century as an adjective from the Latin stem. The noun use 'capacity for future success' appears later.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪以拉丁词干构成形容词 potential。指“未来成功的潜力”的名词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The -ly adverb is formed on the adjective and spreads in scientific and journalistic prose, where claims need hedging.
items.cn: -ly 副词由该形容词构成，在科学与新闻写作中扩散，因为这些文体需要为论断留余地。

items.en: Physics fixes the meaning in potential energy and potential difference, where the quantity is real but unrealized.
items.cn: 物理学在势能与电势差中固定了词义：该量真实存在但尚未实现。

note.en: The look-alike group all contains pot- from potis or from a different root; the near-meaning group shares the idea of possibility but differs in strength.
note.cn: 形近组都含 pot-，或同出 potis，或另有来源；近义组都表“可能”，差别在可能性强度。

entries.definition: existing as a capacity rather than as an act. The adjective modifies a noun; the adverb modifies a whole claim.
entries.definitionCN: 潜在的；潜力。形容词修饰名词，副词修饰整个论断。

entries.definition: strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument. It states present power, not future possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 强效的；有力的。它陈述当下的力量，不是未来的可能。

entries.definition: safe to drink. It looks close but comes from Latin potare 'to drink', not from posse.
entries.definitionCN: 可饮用的。它外形接近，但来自拉丁 potare“喝”，并非 posse。

entries.definition: perhaps; used for plain uncertainty. It is more neutral and less technical than potentially.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；可能。用于一般的不确定，比 potentially 更中性、更少术语色彩。

entries.definition: in a way that can be imagined even if unlikely. It often signals a distant possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象地。即使不太可能也能想到，常暗示较远的可能性。

entries.definition: as may reasonably be supposed. It reports an inference from evidence, not a bare possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 大概；据推测。它报告基于证据的推断，不是单纯的可能。

entries.definition: as can be supported by argument. It hedges a judgment, while potentially hedges a prediction.
entries.definitionCN: 可以说是。它为判断留余地，而 potentially 为预测留余地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: potent- is the stem of 'having power', so potentially means 'with power still held in reserve'.
normal.cn: potent- 是“有力量”的词干，所以 potentially 意为“力量还握在手里未用”。

normal.en: Potential energy in physics is the cleanest model: the energy is there, the movement has not started.
normal.cn: 物理学的势能是最清楚的模型：能量在那里，运动还没开始。

normal.en: In warnings, potentially harmful and potentially fatal pair with the same hedging job.
normal.cn: 在警示语中，可能有危害与可能致命承担同样的留余地功能。

normal.en: Potential plus -ly keeps the adjective visible, so the adverb never claims more than the adjective does.
normal.cn: potential 加 -ly 仍看得见形容词，所以副词声称的绝不超过形容词。

normal.en: The paired noun is potential: a player with potential is one whose value is not yet shown.
normal.cn: 对应名词是 potential：有潜力的选手就是价值尚未展现的人。

abstract.en: Picture a seed in a drawer: the tree is fully possible and completely absent at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里的一颗种子：那棵树既完全可能，又完全不在。

abstract.en: Picture a door that is unlocked but has never been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没锁、却从未被推开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a battery on a shelf: voltage is present, current is not flowing.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上的一节电池：电压在，电流没走。

examples.en: The virus is potentially more contagious than earlier variants.
examples.cn: 这种病毒可能比早期变种更具传染性。

examples.en: She is potentially the best candidate, but she has not applied.
examples.cn: 她可能是最佳人选，但她还没申请。

examples.en: Potentially, the new method could cut costs by a third.
examples.cn: 从可能性上说，新方法能把成本削减三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破摊子里”音近 potentially：破摊子里也许藏着好东西——只是“有可能” → potentially 潜在地

root: 拉丁 posse“能够”（potis esse 的缩合）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“力量、能力”；potential + -ly 构成副词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower the certainty of a statement while keeping the thing described fully real.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在降低陈述的确定性，同时让所描述之物保持真实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed holding a tree that has not grown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子，里面装着还没长出的树。

branches.en: HEDGING: the everyday possibility claim and the debater's hedge both keep the statement open to revision.
branches.cn: 留余地：日常的可能性陈述与辩论中的模糊限制，都让论断保留修改空间。

branches.en: CAPACITY HELD: a strong team and an unused market are both value that exists before it is spent.
branches.cn: 握有的能力：强队与未开发市场都是尚未花掉就已存在的价值。

branches.en: WARNING: risk language names a danger without having to prove it.
branches.cn: 警示：风险语言指出危险，而不必先证明危险。

branches.en: GRAMMATICAL STANCE: scientific inference and grammar teaching both treat the word as a marker of lowered certainty.
branches.cn: 语法立场：科学推论与语法教学都把这个词当作降低确定性的标记。

branches.en: PHYSICS: potential energy and potential difference give the metaphor a measurable form.
branches.cn: 物理学：势能与电势差给这个比喻一个可测量的形态。

intro.en: Potentially is built from the Latin stem potent- plus the English suffix -ly. The -ia and -ia/-cy nouns and the -ent adjective belong to the same family.
intro.cn: potentially 由拉丁词干 potent- 加英语后缀 -ly 构成。-ia 名词、-cy 名词与 -ent 形容词同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin connects potis 'able' to posse 'be able' and potens 'able', from which potentia and English potent derive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把 potis“有能力的”、posse“能够”、potens“有能力的”串起来，potentia 与英语 potent 由此而来。

items.meaningCN: 潜在的；潜力（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: We have a potential buyer for the site.
items.exampleCN: 这块地有一位潜在买家。

items.meaningCN: 潜在地；有可能地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这一变化可能意义重大。

items.meaningCN: 强效的；有力的（分词词干作形容词）

items.example: The potency of the drug declines with heat.

items.meaning: to increase the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 增强药效（-iate 动词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 该化合物增强了抗生素的效果。

items.example: The agency was impotent against the cartel.
items.exampleCN: 该机构对这个卡特尔无能为力。

items.example: The novel gives its ruler omnipotent powers.
items.exampleCN: 小说赋予统治者全能的力量。

items.meaning: dominant in inheritance, a genetics term
items.meaningCN: 遗传上优先显性的（pre-“在前”+ potent）
items.example: A prepotent gene masks the weaker one.
items.exampleCN: 优先显性的基因会掩盖较弱的那一个。

latinEntries.meaning: to be able, to have power

definition_zh: 调整；调节装置；适应过程；心理调适；保险理算；工资或价格的调整；校准；对……的适应
definition_en: a small change made to something so that it fits, works correctly, or suits a new situation
core_image: 把歪了的桌腿一点点垫平：拧动螺栓，让物件重新贴合地面
scene: 车间的老机床跑偏了，师傅停下车床，俯身去拧底座上的螺栓。 He made a small adjustment to the base of the machine and the vibration stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 adjustment 是「调整动作」（第 1 个义项：为使某物更合适而做的小改动）；句意为他对机器底座做了小幅调整，震动便停止了。

pos.zh: 名词：调整；调节装置；适应；理算

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的动词，义为「调整；调节；适应」
由 adjust 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可调整的」
由 adjust 加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「调节器；理算员」
由前缀 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整；再适应」
由前缀 mal-「坏」加本词构成，义为「适应不良；失调」

senses.title: A small change made to a thing
senses.titleCN: 调整动作：对物件的小改动
senses.definition: a small change made to a device, plan, or arrangement so that it works or fits better
senses.definitionCN: 为使装置、计划或安排运转得更好或更贴合而做的小改动
senses.example: A slight adjustment to the seat made the long drive comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 对座椅做了轻微调整，长途驾驶就舒服了。
senses.why: The core image is a tilted table leg being padded: a small turn of the bolt, and the thing sits level again.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是垫平歪斜的桌腿：螺栓只转了一点，物件便重新稳稳落地。

senses.title: A part that regulates a mechanism
senses.titleCN: 调节装置：机器上的可调部件
senses.definition: a part or mechanism used to set, tune, or regulate a machine or instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用来设定、微调或调节机器、仪器的部件或机构
senses.example: Turn the adjustment at the side of the lamp to change its angle.
senses.exampleCN: 转动灯侧面的调节装置就能改变角度。
senses.why: If the act of turning can level a thing, the part you turn becomes the adjustment itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然「拧动」能让物件归位，那么被拧动的那个部件本身也就被叫作 adjustment。

senses.title: The process of settling into a new situation
senses.titleCN: 适应过程：迁入新环境的过渡
senses.definition: the process of getting used to a new place, job, school, or set of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐熟悉新地方、新工作、新学校或新条件的过程
senses.example: Moving abroad involves a long period of adjustment.
senses.exampleCN: 移居国外需要一段很长的适应期。
senses.why: The table leg is now a person: the small changes are made inside a life until it fits its new ground.
senses.whyCN: 这里的桌腿换成了人：一点一点的改变发生在生活内部，直到它与新的地面贴合。

senses.title: Emotional adjustment
senses.titleCN: 心理调适：情绪上的重新平衡
senses.definition: the mental process of coping with stress, loss, or a changed circumstance
senses.definitionCN: 应对压力、失落或环境变化时的心理调适过程
senses.example: Counsellors help students with the emotional adjustment to college.
senses.exampleCN: 辅导员帮助学生应对进入大学后的情绪调适。
senses.why: When the thing being levelled is the mind, the change is made in feelings rather than in wood or metal.
senses.whyCN: 当被垫平的对象是心灵时，改动就发生在情绪里，而不是木头或金属里。

senses.title: Insurance loss adjustment
senses.titleCN: 保险理算：核定赔付金额
senses.definition: the assessment of an insurance claim in order to decide how much the insurer must pay
senses.definitionCN: 对保险索赔进行核定，以确定保险人应赔付多少
senses.example: The insurance adjustment reduced the claim by half.
senses.exampleCN: 保险理算把索赔金额削减了一半。
senses.why: A damaged claim is balanced against a policy: the assessor turns the figures until the two sides agree.
senses.whyCN: 受损的索赔要与保单相衡：理算员反复拨动数字，直到两边对得上。

senses.title: An official change in wages or prices
senses.definition: an official change in the level of pay, prices, or benefits, usually made at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 对工资、价格或福利水平的正式调整，通常按固定周期进行
senses.example: The annual wage adjustment raised every salary by three percent.
senses.exampleCN: 年度工资调整把每份薪水都提高了三个百分点。
senses.why: Whole figures can be levelled too: the same small turn is applied to a rate that has drifted out of line.
senses.whyCN: 整组数字也能被垫平：同一个「拧一拧」的动作，用在已经偏离轨道的费率上。

senses.title: Calibration of an instrument
senses.definition: the act of setting an instrument or measuring device so that its readings are accurate
senses.definitionCN: 调整仪器或测量装置，使其读数重新准确的动作
senses.example: The adjustment of the scale took two careful hours.
senses.exampleCN: 校准这台天平花了两个小时，做得很仔细。
senses.why: Here the standard is accuracy itself: the instrument is turned until its pointer and the true measure coincide.
senses.whyCN: 这里的标准就是精确：仪器被反复调校，直到指针与真实量值重合。

senses.title: Adjustment to a physical condition
senses.titleCN: 对……的适应：与特定条件相合
senses.definition: in the phrase adjustment to, the process of becoming suited to a particular physical or external condition
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 adjustment to，表示逐渐与某种身体条件或外部条件相适应的过程
senses.example: The adjustment to high altitude can cause headaches at first.
senses.exampleCN: 初到高海拔地区时，对环境的适应可能引起头痛。
senses.why: The phrase names the ground the thing must fit: adjustment to altitude, to cold, to a new rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语点明了物件必须贴合的那块地面：适应海拔、适应寒冷、适应新的作息。

intro.en: Adjustment is the noun built on adjust, a verb borrowed from Old French and usually explained through the idea of making something exact.
intro.cn: adjustment 是在动词 adjust 之上加名词后缀构成的名词；adjust 借自古法语，一般解释为「使某物变得精确、合适」。

items.en: The adverb juxta meant 'near, close by', from a root often connected with joining; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 juxta 意为「在近旁」，其词根常被认为与「连接」有关；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Old French adjuster, also written ajouster, meant 'to arrange, set in order'. It is usually analysed as a- plus juste 'just, exact', though a link to Latin juxta has also been proposed.
items.cn: 古法语 adjuster（也写作 ajouster）意为「安排、整理」。一般认为它由 a- 加 juste「公正、精确」构成，也有学者把它联系到拉丁语 juxta。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fourteenth or fifteenth century with the sense 'to arrange, settle, harmonize'; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四或十五世纪进入英语，意为「安排、安顿、使协调」；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun adjustment joins the verb to the French and Latin suffix -ment, which marks an act or its result.
items.cn: 名词 adjustment 由动词加法语、拉丁语来源的后缀 -ment 构成，该后缀表示动作或其结果。

items.en: The noun widened from arranging objects to adapting people, tuning machines, changing pay rates, and settling insurance claims.
items.cn: 这个名词从「整理物件」扩展到人的适应、机器的调校、工资的变动以及保险索赔的核定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same adjust base; the near-meaning group gathers other words for change, fit, and measurement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 adjust 词基构成的一族词；近义组收其他表示改变、适配与测量的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to change something slightly so that it fits or works better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整、调节」，即小幅改变某物使其更合适或运转更好。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to be changed or set in different positions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调整的」，指能够改变或调到不同位置。

entries.definition: A noun for a person who assesses insurance claims, or a device that regulates something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理算员」或「调节器」，指核定索赔的人或起调节作用的装置。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to adjust again after a first change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新调整」，指在第一次改动之后再次调节。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a failure to adapt to one's circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应不良、失调」，指未能与所处环境相适应。

entries.definition: The process of changing in order to suit a new environment; broader and often slower than an adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，强调为适合新环境而改变，范围更宽、过程常更慢。

entries.definition: A change made to something, often a more deliberate and structural one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修改、改动」，通常指更有意为之、幅度更大的改动。

entries.definition: The exact setting of an instrument against a standard, narrower than adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「校准」，指依标准精确设定仪器，范围比 adjustment 更窄。

entries.definition: A change in form or character, with no idea of fitting or tuning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改变、改动」，只强调形态或性质变化，不含「调适、校准」的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French base and the word family that grows from adjust.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古法语词基，以及由 adjust 长出的整个词族。

normal.en: The verb adjust is borrowed from Old French, and the noun simply adds -ment.
normal.cn: 动词 adjust 借自古法语，名词只是在它后面加 -ment。

normal.en: Juste inside adjust carries exactness: to adjust is to make something exact.
normal.cn: adjust 里的 juste 带着「精确」的意思：adjust 就是把某物调到精确。

normal.en: Adjustable, adjuster and readjustment keep the same base; only the suffixes differ.
normal.cn: adjustable、adjuster、readjustment 都保留同一个词基，只是后缀不同。

normal.en: A wage adjustment changes pay, while an insurance adjustment settles a claim.
normal.cn: wage adjustment 改变的是工资，insurance adjustment 结清的是索赔。

normal.en: The phrase adjustment to always names the condition that a person or thing must fit.
normal.cn: 短语 adjustment to 总是点明人或物必须去贴合的那个条件。

abstract.en: Picture an old table with one short leg: a few turns of the bolt, and the top is level again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧桌子有一条短腿：螺栓转几下，桌面就重新水平了。

abstract.en: Change the table for a person in a new city: the same small turns happen inside the life.
abstract.cn: 把桌子换成一个初到新城市的人：同样的小幅转动发生在他的生活里。

abstract.en: Change it again for a scale or a salary: anything out of line can be brought back into line.
abstract.cn: 再把它换成一架天平或一份薪水：任何偏离轨道的对象都能被调回轨道。

examples.en: A slight adjustment to the seat made the whole journey pleasant.
examples.cn: 对座椅稍作调整，整段旅程就变得舒适了。

examples.en: The company announced a wage adjustment for all staff.
examples.cn: 公司宣布对所有员工进行工资调整。

examples.en: Her adjustment to the new school took most of the autumn.
examples.cn: 她花了整个秋天来适应新学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额贾斯特门特」——师傅蹲下身，拧一拧、垫一垫，机器就重新合身了

root: adjust 借自古法语 adjuster「安排、整理」，一般认为由 a-「向」加 juste「公正、精确」构成，juste 又来自拉丁语 justus，与 ius「权利、法」相关；也有解释把它联系到拉丁语 juxta「在近旁」。再加名词后缀 -ment 构成 adjustment。更早的印欧词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses apply one small act of levelling: to an object, to its regulating part, to a person settling in, to the mind, to a claim, to a rate, to an instrument, and to a specific condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在施加同一个「小幅归位」的动作：用在物件、调节部件、人的安顿、心理、索赔、费率、仪器，以及某个特定条件上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tilted leg is padded a little at a time until the whole thing stands level.
core.cn: 核心意象：歪斜的桌腿被一点一点垫平，直到整个物件重新站稳。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a small change and the part that is turned to make it hold.
branches.cn: 物件线：一次小改动，以及被拧动的那个部件。

branches.en: THE PERSON: getting used to a place, or suiting a particular physical condition.
branches.cn: 人的线：适应一个新地方，或与某种身体条件相合。

branches.en: THE MIND: the same levelling happens in feelings rather than in wood or metal.
branches.cn: 心理线：同样的归位发生在情绪里，而不是木头或金属里。

branches.en: THE MONEY: claims and pay rates are brought back into line by the same small turns.
branches.cn: 金钱线：索赔与工资费率也靠同样的小幅拨动被调回轨道。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: accuracy is the ground, and the pointer is turned until it touches it.
branches.cn: 仪器线：精确就是那块地面，指针被调到与它相接。

intro.en: Adjustment is a French borrowing dressed with Latin suffixes; the word is not built from English parts alone.
intro.cn: adjustment 是借自法语的词，再加上拉丁语来源的后缀；它并非只用英语部件构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin words behind the family are juxta, justus and ius, all recorded; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词族背后的拉丁词 juxta、justus、ius 都有文献记录，只有更早的词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It appears in administrare and in French a-.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在拉丁语 administrare 与法语 a- 之中。

items.example: The word was taken into English as just.
items.exampleCN: 这个词被英语吸收为 just。

items.example: Adjust the mirror before you drive.

items.exampleCN: 它把 adjust 构成 adjustment。

items.example: It is the source of the idea of placing things side by side.
items.exampleCN: 它是「把事物并排放置」这一观念的来源。

definition_zh: 四倍的；四重的
definition_en: four times as much, or having four parts
core_image: 一根细线折成四层，厚度一下变成原来的四倍
scene: 更换设备后产量增长了四倍。 Output rose fourfold after the equipment was replaced.
sceneCN: 这里 fourfold 是「四倍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：更换设备后产量增长了四倍。

senses.title: Four times as much
senses.definition: four times as large or as much
senses.definitionCN: 大小为原来的四倍
senses.example: Output rose fourfold after the equipment was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 更换设备后产量增长了四倍。
senses.why: This is the basic multiplier sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的倍数义项。

senses.title: Having four parts
senses.definition: made of four parts or layers
senses.definitionCN: 由四部分或四层组成的
senses.example: The answer has a fourfold structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个答案有四重结构。
senses.why: Folding a thing four times gives four layers.
senses.whyCN: 把东西折四次就得到四层。

intro.en: Fourfold joins four with the old suffix -fold.
intro.cn: fourfold 由 four 加上古老后缀 -fold 构成。

items.en: Feowerfeald meant fourfold.
items.cn: feowerfeald 意为四倍的。

items.en: The form became fourfold.
items.cn: 词形演变为 fourfold。

items.en: The word measured increase in business.
items.cn: 这个词用来衡量商业增长。

items.en: It also described four-part structures.
items.cn: 它也用来描述四部分的结构。

items.en: The suffix -fold named many multiples.
items.cn: 后缀 -fold 构成许多倍数词。

note.en: Fourfold is compared with similar-looking words and with multiplier words.
note.cn: 把 fourfold 与形近词以及倍数词作比较。

to bend something over
coming after the third
to become four times as much
a number that contains another several times
one thickness of material

normalIntro.cn: fourfold 意为翻了四倍。

normal.en: Output rose fourfold after the equipment was replaced.
normal.cn: 更换设备后产量增长了四倍。

normal.en: The company saw a fourfold increase.
normal.cn: 公司经历了四倍的增长。

normal.en: The investment gave a fourfold return.
normal.cn: 这笔投资带来了四倍回报。

normal.en: The answer has a fourfold structure.

normal.en: Sales grew fourfold in two years.
normal.cn: 两年内销量增长到四倍。

abstract.en: Fourfold is one step becoming four.
abstract.cn: 四倍是一步变成四步。

abstract.en: Growth can be measured and still surprise.
abstract.cn: 增长可以被衡量，却依然令人惊讶。

abstract.en: Folding adds layers without adding width.
abstract.cn: 折叠增加层数，却不增加宽度。

examples.en: Output rose fourfold after the equipment was replaced.
examples.cn: 更换设备后产量增长了四倍。

examples.en: The company saw a fourfold increase.
examples.cn: 公司经历了四倍的增长。

examples.en: The answer has a fourfold structure.
examples.cn: 这个答案有四重结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: four（四）加 -fold（倍、层）：数量翻到四倍，结构叠成四层，都是 fourfold。

root: 源自古英语 feowerfeald，由 feower（四）加 -feald（倍、层）构成，核心义「四倍或四重」。

sensesIntro.en: Fourfold means four times as much or having four parts.
sensesIntro.cn: fourfold 意为四倍的或四重的。

core.en: One amount multiplied by four.
core.cn: 一份数量乘以四。

branches.en: Production grows to four times.
branches.cn: 产量增长到四倍。

branches.en: The paper is folded into four layers.
branches.cn: 纸被折成四层。

branches.en: The return is four times the cost.
branches.cn: 回报是成本的四倍。

branches.en: Multiplication and folding both repeat four.
branches.cn: 倍数与折叠都重复了四次。

branches.en: Layers make thickness visible.
branches.cn: 层数让厚度可见。

intro.en: Fourfold belongs to the four family of number words.
intro.cn: fourfold 属于 four 这一数词家族。

latinIntro.en: Fourfold is Germanic; Latin quadruplus, fourfold, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fourfold 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 quadruplus（四倍的）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 他们报告了四倍的增长。

items.example: The plan promised a fourfold return.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划承诺四倍回报。

definition_zh: 延长；拉长；使持续更久
definition_en: to make something last longer in time, or to stretch it out in length
core_image: 两只手抓住一根绳子，往两头慢慢拉，绳子变得更长
scene: 会谈已经拖到深夜，桌上的人都看着钟，谁也不愿先起身。 The chairman refused to prolong the discussion and closed the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里取「延长、使持续更久」的意思（第 1 个义项：让某件事持续更久）；句意为主席不愿再把讨论拖长，于是宣布散会。

pos.zh: 延长；拉长；使（时间）持续更久

derivatives.zh: 由 prolong 加 -ation 构成，义为「延长；延期」
由 prolong 的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「持续很久的；长时间的」

senses.title: To make something last longer
senses.definition: to make an event, a state or a period continue for a longer time
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件、状态或时期持续更久
senses.example: Nothing could prolong the summer beyond September.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能让夏天延续到九月之后。
senses.why: Latin longus means long, and the prefix pro- pushes outward, so the word starts from stretching something out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 longus 意为「长」，前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以这个词的起点是「把东西往外拉长」。

senses.title: To make a hard experience drag on
senses.definition: to keep an unpleasant situation or feeling going when it could end
senses.definitionCN: 在本可结束时让不愉快的处境或感受继续下去
senses.example: Refusing to decide only prolonged the uncertainty for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 迟迟不做决定，只是让所有人的不确定感拖得更久。
senses.why: If length can be added to anything, it can be added to pain, so the word often carries the sense of needlessly extending what people want to end.
senses.whyCN: 既然长度可以加在任何东西上，也能加在痛苦上，于是这个词常带「把人们盼着结束的事无谓地拖长」的意味。

senses.title: To stretch something out in length
senses.definition: to extend something in physical length, a formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 从物理长度上把某物拉长，属正式或文学用法
senses.example: The low sun prolonged every shadow across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 低垂的太阳把田野上每道影子都拉得很长。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply long, and when the object is a shadow or a line the word returns to that plain idea of length.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「长」，当宾语是影子或线条时，这个词又回到最朴素的长度概念。

intro.en: Prolong joins a Latin prefix of outward movement to the Latin word for long, and French carried the verb into English.
intro.cn: prolong 把表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀接在表示「长」的拉丁词上，再由法语把动词带进英语。

items.en: The prefix pro- meant forward or outward, and longus meant long, so the pair pictured something drawn out at length.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向前、向外，形容词 longus 表示长，两者合起来就是「往外拉长」。

items.en: Prolongare meant to lengthen, to draw out, and it was used of both time and physical extent.
items.cn: prolongare 意为加长、拉长，时间和空间长度都能用它。

items.en: Old French prolonger kept the verb's sense of making something last or reach further.
items.cn: 古法语 prolonger 保留了「使某物更持久、伸得更远」的意思。

items.en: Middle English took the verb and used it mostly in the sense of adding time to something.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个动词，多指给某事加上时间。

items.en: Modern English uses prolong mainly for time, and keeps the physical sense in literary descriptions of light, shadows and lines.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prolong 主要用于时间，物理意义上的拉长则多见于对光、影与线条的文学描写。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for long; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for adding extent or time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「长」形容词上的词；近义组收表示加长长度或时间的动词。

entries.definition: To make something longer, especially in shape.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变长，尤指形状上的拉长。

entries.definition: Long life, or the length of a life.
The distance east or west measured in degrees.
entries.definitionCN: 以度数计量的东西方向距离；经度。

entries.definition: To make something longer or larger in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上使某物更长或更大。

entries.definition: To become or make longer.
To pull something so that it covers more space.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉展到占更多空间。

entries.definition: To make something take longer than necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事拖得比必要的时间更长。

normalIntro.en: The word is a rope being pulled longer, and its family keeps returning to length and to time added on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一根被拉长的绳子，同族词反复回到「长度」和「被加上去的时间」。

normal.en: Latin longus also gives English longitude, so the idea of length sits inside prolong from the start.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 longus 还给英语带来 longitude，所以「长度」这个观念从一开始就在 prolong 里面。

normal.en: The prefix pro- pushes outward, so the rope leaves the hand rather than staying still.
normal.cn: 前缀 pro- 表示向外推，所以绳子是离开手心、被拉出去的。

normal.en: Prolongation adds -ation to the verb: the act of making something longer.
normal.cn: prolongation 在动词后加 -ation，指「使某物变长」这件事。

normal.en: We prolong life, meetings and agony, but the word often leans towards what people already wish would end.
normal.cn: 我们说延长寿命、延长会议、延长痛苦，而这个词常偏向人们本来就盼着结束的事。

normal.en: The adjective prolonged comes straight from the past participle and describes anything that has been drawn out.
normal.cn: 形容词 prolonged 直接来自过去分词，描述任何被拉长了的事物。

abstract.en: Anything measured in time can be stretched, which is why a word for length ends up meaning delay.
abstract.cn: 凡是用时间衡量的东西都能被拉长，所以一个表示长度的词最后也指拖延。

abstract.en: Prolonging is rarely neutral: adding time to something people want to end is adding weight to it.
abstract.cn: 延长很少是中性的：给人们盼着结束的事加上时间，等于给它加上重量。

abstract.en: A shadow and a meeting can share one verb because both are lines that someone draws out.
abstract.cn: 影子和会议能共用一个动词，因为两者都是被谁拉长的一根线。

examples.en: Regular exercise can prolong your life.
examples.cn: 经常锻炼可以延长寿命。

examples.en: They prolonged the meeting by arguing over details.
examples.cn: 他们为细节争论，把会议拖长了。

examples.en: A prolonged drought has dried up the river.
examples.cn: 长久干旱使这条河干涸了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若龙」——往前一扑像条长龙，越拉越长，就是延长。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、向外）+ longus（长）构成 prolongare，本义「往外拉长」，经古法语 prolonger 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is stretching something outward; the senses divide into added time, needlessly added suffering, and the older physical stretching.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西往外拉长」；义项分成加上的时间、无谓拖长的痛苦，以及更古老的物理拉长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling a rope apart so that it grows longer and longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手抓住一根绳子往两头拉，绳子越拉越长。

branches.en: a meeting that nobody wants to end
branches.cn: 谁都不愿意散的会议

branches.en: a waiting room where the clock barely moves
branches.cn: 钟几乎不走的候诊室

branches.en: shadows stretching across a field at sunset
branches.cn: 日落时横过田野的长影

branches.en: a low sun drawing a long line of shadow
branches.cn: 低垂的太阳拖出一道长长的影子

branches.en: a decision put off until the worry grows
branches.cn: 被一再推迟、让焦虑加长的决定

intro.en: A Latin prefix of outward movement and the Latin adjective for long hold the word together; French supplied the verb form that English borrowed.
intro.cn: 表示向外运动的拉丁语前缀和表示「长」的拉丁语形容词共同支撑这个词，英语借入的动词形式来自法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin longus, long, and the verb prolongare, to lengthen, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 longus（长）与动词 prolongare（加长）是英语这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 谁（宾格）；…的那个人（宾格关系代词）
definition_en: the object form of who, used after a verb or a preposition and in careful relative clauses
core_image: 一只手把某个人指给另一个人看，被指的人站在前面，动作落在他身上
scene: 律师翻着名单，问在场的人这封信究竟寄给谁，问到的人却一声不响。 To whom should I address this letter?
sceneCN: 这里 whom 是「谁（宾格）」（第 1 个义项：作动词或介词的宾语时用的形式）；句意为我该把这封信寄给谁呢。那只把动作引到某人身上的指向，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: Asking for the object
senses.definition: the object form of who, used when the unknown person receives the action of the verb
senses.definitionCN: who 的宾格形式，在未知的人承受动作时使用
senses.example: Whom did you meet at the station?
senses.exampleCN: 你在车站遇见了谁？
senses.why: English once kept a full set of case endings, and this is the one survivor in common use.
senses.whyCN: 英语曾保留完整的格词尾，而这是日常用法中唯一存活下来的那个。

senses.title: After a preposition
senses.definition: used directly after a preposition such as to, with or for, where who is not allowed in careful style
senses.definitionCN: 直接用于 to、with、for 等介词之后，在严谨文体中此处不用 who
senses.example: To whom should I address this letter?
senses.exampleCN: 我该把这封信寄给谁呢？
senses.why: A preposition needs an object right after it, and the old object form still fills that slot.
senses.whyCN: 介词后面需要宾语，而这个古老的宾格形式仍能占住那个位置。

senses.title: The relative object form
senses.definition: in a relative clause, referring back to a person who is the object of the clause
senses.definitionCN: 在关系从句中回指一个人，而此人在从句里是宾语
senses.example: The painter whom we met last year has died.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去年见过的那位画家去世了。
senses.why: When the person is acted upon inside the clause, careful writers choose whom.
senses.whyCN: 当此人在从句中承受动作时，严谨的作者会选用 whom。

senses.title: In formal lists and counts
senses.definition: in formal writing, used after of to pick a group out of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 在正式书面语中放在 of 之后，表示从更大群体中挑出的一群
senses.example: The team has three members, two of whom are engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队有三名成员，其中两名是工程师。
senses.why: Counting people with of needs the object form, so the word survives in statistics and reports.
senses.whyCN: 用 of 来数人需要宾格，所以这个词在统计与报告中仍然存活。

intro.en: Whom is the old dative and accusative of who, from Old English hwam, the case forms of hwa.
intro.cn: whom 是 who 古老的与格和宾格形式，来自古英语 hwa 的格形式 hwam。

items.en: The question stem took different endings for subject, object and possessor in every old Germanic language.
items.cn: 在所有古老的日耳曼语言中，疑问词干都会按主语、宾语、所有者换上不同词尾。

items.en: Hwa was the subject form and hwam the form used for the object and after prepositions.
items.cn: hwa 是主格，hwam 用于宾语以及介词之后。

items.en: The ending weakened to whom, and careful writers kept it while speech began to drop it.
items.cn: 词尾弱化为 whom，严谨的作者仍保留它，而口语已开始丢弃。

items.en: After a preposition whom stayed firm in writing, as in to whom and of whom.
items.cn: 在介词之后，whom 在书面语中稳稳站住，如 to whom、of whom。

items.en: Today spoken English usually says who, and whom is a mark of careful or dated style.
items.cn: 如今口语通常说 who，而 whom 是严谨或略显陈旧文体的标志。

note.en: The first group gathers the other case forms of the same stem, the second the plain relative words that can replace it.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他格形式，第二组收可以替代它的朴素关系词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same word.
The possessive form, asking about ownership.
The object form of whoever.
A sudden wish, unrelated in origin.
A plain relative word, no case endings needed.
A relative word for things rather than people.
An unnamed person, often the answer to whom.

normalIntro.en: Whom is who with an m, and the m is a memory of the old case endings English once had.
normalIntro.cn: whom 就是带 m 的 who，这个 m 是英语曾经那套格词尾留下的记忆。

normal.en: Him and them end in m too, and all three are object forms.
normal.cn: him 和 them 也是 m 结尾，三者都是宾格。

normal.en: If him fits the gap, then whom fits as well.
normal.cn: 如果那个空里能放 him，那么也能放 whom。

normal.en: After to, with, of and for, whom is the safe choice in writing.
normal.cn: 写在 to、with、of、for 之后，whom 是稳妥的选择。

normal.en: Two of whom are engineers: the of makes the case clear.
normal.cn: two of whom are engineers 中的 of 把格说得很清楚。

normal.en: In speech, who has almost taken over, so whom is mostly ink.
normal.cn: 口语里 who 几乎接管了一切，所以 whom 多半只出现在纸上。

abstract.en: Feel an action landing on a person who does nothing back.
abstract.cn: 感觉一个动作落在某人身上，而那人毫无反击。

abstract.en: See a finger pointed by one person at another.
abstract.cn: 看见一个人把手指向另一个人。

abstract.en: Hear a name asked for by a preposition.
abstract.cn: 听见介词在追问一个名字。

examples.en: The lecturer whom everyone respected has retired.
examples.cn: 那位人人尊敬的讲师已经退休了。

examples.en: With whom did you travel to the north?
examples.cn: 你和谁一起去了北方？

examples.en: Ten students took part, most of whom came from the village.
examples.cn: 十名学生参加，其中大多数来自村里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呼姆」——呼一声姆，姆被叫过去，是被动的那个，所以是宾格。

root: 日耳曼语疑问词干 → 古英语 hwam（宾格、与格）→ 中古英语 whom → 现代英语 whom；同族有 who、whose、whomever。

sensesIntro.en: The word marks a person who receives the action, keeps that work after a preposition, carries it into relative clauses, and finally into formal counts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词标记承受动作的人，在介词后保持这一功能，再带进关系从句，最后进入正式的计数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing at someone, the action falling on that person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指指向某人，动作落在那人身上。

branches.en: The question branch: whom did you meet at the station.
branches.cn: 发问分支：你在车站遇见了谁。

branches.en: The preposition branch: to whom should I write.
branches.cn: 介词分支：我该写给谁。

branches.en: The relative branch: the painter whom we met.
branches.cn: 关系分支：我们见过的那位画家。

branches.en: The counting branch: two of whom are engineers.
branches.cn: 计数分支：其中两位是工程师。

branches.en: The object branch: him fits, so whom fits.
branches.cn: 宾语分支：能放 him，也就能放 whom。

intro.en: Whom is not built with a suffix but is a case form of the question stem, and it feeds the compound whomever.
intro.cn: whom 不是用后缀构成的，而是疑问词干的一个格形式，它还派生出复合词 whomever。

latinIntro.en: The native stem has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below show how the same case work is done with quis and quem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个本土词干没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目展示 quis、quem 如何承担同样的格功能。

items.example: The preposition fixes the case in writing.
items.exampleCN: 介词在书面语中固定了口格。

items.example: It survives in reports and lists.
items.exampleCN: 它存活于报告与名单中。

items.meaning: which person to do something with
items.example: A small clause with an infinitive.
items.exampleCN: 一个带动词不定式的小句。

items.example: It pairs the case form with ever.
items.exampleCN: 它把宾格形式与 ever 配对。

latinEntries.example: It is the exact Latin accusative of quis.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 quis 的拉丁语宾格的精确对应。

definition_zh: 微弱地；隐约地；虚弱地
definition_en: in a weak or dim way; barely and not clearly; with little strength or effort
core_image: 声音轻得像从很远的地方飘来
scene: 远处隐约传来音乐声。 Music could be heard faintly in the distance.
sceneCN: 这里 faintly 是「隐约地、微弱地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：远处隐约传来音乐声。

senses.title: Weakly
senses.definition: in a weak or dim way, so that it is hard to notice
senses.definitionCN: 以微弱或暗淡的方式，难以察觉
senses.example: The lamp glowed faintly in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在黑暗中发出微弱的光。
senses.why: The base sense is a low level of light or sound.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是光或声处于很低水平。

senses.title: Barely
senses.definition: only just and not clearly
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅、勉强而不清晰
senses.example: The path was faintly visible through the mist.
senses.exampleCN: 透过薄雾，小路隐约可见。
senses.why: A weak signal is barely enough to be noticed.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号只是勉强够被察觉。

senses.title: With little strength
senses.definition: with little strength or effort
senses.definitionCN: 力气或用力很少地
senses.example: She smiled faintly and closed her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她无力地笑了笑，闭上了眼睛。
senses.why: The weak signal becomes weak human action.
senses.whyCN: 微弱信号转为人动作的无力度。

intro.en: Faintly is faint plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: faintly 由 faint 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Feint means weak or pretended.
items.cn: feint 意为虚弱的或假装的。

items.en: Faint becomes an English adjective.
items.cn: faint 成为英语形容词。

items.en: The adverb faintly appears in writing.
items.cn: 副词 faintly 出现在书面语中。

items.en: Faintly describes dim light and distant sound.
items.cn: 十九世纪 faintly 描述暗光与远声。

items.en: Faintly also describes weak smiles and voices.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faintly 也描述无力的微笑与声音。

note.en: Faintly means weakly; saintly means like a saint.
note.cn: faintly 是微弱地，saintly 则是圣洁的。

entries.definition: weak or unclear
very holy or good
a deceptive movement
with little light or clarity
with little strength
not clearly or exactly

normalIntro.en: Faintly lowers the strength of a light, a sound, or a smile.
normalIntro.cn: faintly 把光、声或微笑的强度调低。

normal.en: A star shone faintly above the hills.
normal.cn: 一颗星在山丘上方微弱地闪烁。

normal.en: He could faintly hear the radio.
normal.cn: 他隐约能听到收音机声。

normal.en: The old writing was faintly legible.
normal.cn: 旧字迹勉强可辨。

normal.en: She smiled faintly at the compliment.
normal.cn: 她听到赞美淡淡一笑。

normal.en: The room smelled faintly of coffee.
normal.cn: 房间里有淡淡的咖啡味。

abstract.en: Picture a signal too soft to fill the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个弱到填不满房间的信号。

abstract.en: Imagine a line drawn with a dry pencil.
abstract.cn: 想象用干铅笔画出的一条线。

abstract.en: Think of a smile that lifts only the corners of the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象只牵动嘴角的微笑。

examples.en: The outline of the mountain was faintly visible.
examples.cn: 山峰的轮廓隐约可见。

examples.en: She spoke faintly after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后她有气无力地说话。

examples.en: The perfume smelled faintly of roses.
examples.cn: 这香水有淡淡的玫瑰味。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 后缀派生
dict_mnemonic.text: faint（微弱的）+ -ly（副词后缀）= faintly（微弱地），与 slowly、softly 的构成方式相同。

root: faintly 由 faint（微弱的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，源头可追溯到古法语 feint 与拉丁语 fingere。

sensesIntro.en: Faintly means weakly, barely, or with little strength.
sensesIntro.cn: faintly 意为微弱地、勉强地，或无力地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signal that reaches you only just.
core.cn: 核心意象：勉强传到你的微弱信号。

branches.en: The base sense is a low level of light or sound.
branches.cn: 基础义是光或声的低水平。

branches.en: A weak signal is only just noticeable.
branches.cn: 微弱信号只是勉强可察觉。

branches.en: Weak signals become weak human actions.
branches.cn: 微弱信号转为无力的动作。

branches.en: Dim light and distant sound share one softness.
branches.cn: 暗光与远声共享同一种轻柔。

branches.en: Barely visible and barely smiling both lower intensity.
branches.cn: 隐约可见与淡淡一笑都降低了强度。

intro.en: The adverb suffix -ly turns faint into faintly.
intro.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 把 faint 变成 faintly。

latinIntro.en: Faintly inherits the Latin root fingere through French.
latinIntro.cn: faintly 经由法语继承了拉丁词根 fingere。

items.meaning: in a weak or dim way

items.exampleCN: 他听到一个微弱的声音。

items.example: There was not the faintest sound.
The faintness of the signal delayed the call.
The climb is not for the fainthearted.
items.exampleCN: 这次攀登不适合胆小者。

items.example: They walked through a faintly lit hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们走过灯光微弱的大厅。

latinEntries.example: Fingere is the distant source of faint.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fingere 是 faint 的远源。
fictus 解释了 feint 这一分支。

definition_zh: 珠宝；首饰；珠宝类（总称）
definition_en: rings, necklaces, and other ornaments worn as decoration, taken together as a class of objects
core_image: 绒布上摊开一圈金环、一串珠链和几颗嵌在托里的石头
scene: 柜台的灯打得很亮，托盘里一排镶石头的小饰物闪着光。 She keeps her jewellery in a small wooden box.
sceneCN: 这里 jewellery 是「珠宝首饰」（第 1 个义项：作为一类饰物的总称），句意为她把手饰都放在一个小木盒里。画面里的物件：柜台、托盘、木盒。

pos.zh: 名词：珠宝；首饰（不可数的总称）

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，指单颗宝石或一件镶宝石的饰物
由 jewel 加 -er 构成，义为「珠宝商；宝石匠」
由 be- 加 jewel 加 -ed 构成，义为「镶满宝石的」

senses.title: Ornaments worn as a class
senses.definition: rings, necklaces, brooches, and similar ornaments considered together
senses.definitionCN: 戒指、项链、胸针一类饰物合在一起的总称
senses.example: Her jewellery was simple: one ring and a thin chain.
senses.exampleCN: 她的首饰很简单：一枚戒指和一条细链。
senses.why: The word was built as a collective noun, so it names the whole class rather than one item.
senses.whyCN: 这个词天生是集合名词，所以指整类而不是单件。

senses.title: Precious pieces with gems
senses.definition: such ornaments when they hold gold, silver, or cut stones of real value
senses.definitionCN: 指镶有金银或真正宝石、价值较高的饰物
senses.example: The insurance covers the jewellery kept in the safe.
senses.exampleCN: 保险覆盖存放在保险箱里的镶宝首饰。
senses.why: Value is the quality that separates ordinary ornaments from pieces the word most often names.
senses.whyCN: 值钱与否，正是这个词所指对象与普通饰物的分界。

senses.title: The trade and craft
senses.definition: the trade, craft, or industry of making and selling such ornaments
senses.definitionCN: 制作与销售这类饰物的行业或手艺
senses.example: She trained in jewellery before opening her own studio.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学过珠宝工艺，后来才开了自己的工作室。
senses.why: Naming the objects easily slides into naming the business built on them.
senses.whyCN: 指物件很容易就滑向以这些物件为生的行业。

senses.title: Costume ornaments
senses.definition: cheap decorative ornaments made to look like precious ones
senses.definitionCN: 模仿贵重首饰的廉价装饰品
senses.example: The dancers wore bright costume jewellery on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在台上戴着亮闪闪的装饰首饰。
senses.why: Once the word covered all ornaments, cheap imitations could carry it too, usually with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词覆盖所有饰物，廉价的仿品也能用它，通常还要加限定词。

senses.title: A personal collection
senses.definition: the set of such ornaments that one person owns and keeps
senses.definitionCN: 某个人拥有并保存的全部这类饰物
senses.example: She left her jewellery to her granddaughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把首饰留给了孙女。
senses.why: A collective noun naturally comes to mean one household collection.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词很自然地被用来指一户人家的全部收藏。

intro.en: Jewellery is a collective noun built from jewel, and jewel came to English through French from late Latin.
intro.cn: jewellery 是由 jewel 加后缀构成的集合名词，而 jewel 经由法语、从晚期拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin jocale meant a plaything or ornament, from jocus, a jest.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 意为玩物或饰物，源自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.en: Old French turned it into joel or jouel, a precious ornament.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 joel、jouel，指贵重饰物。

items.en: English borrowed it as jewel and added the agent noun jeweller.
items.cn: 英语借作 jewel，并加 -er 造出 jeweller。

items.en: Jewellery was formed from jeweller as a collective noun in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: jewellery 在十八世纪由 jeweller 派生为集合名词。

items.en: American spelling shortened it to jewelry, while British kept jewellery.
items.cn: 美式拼写简作 jewelry，英式保留 jewellery。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jewel stem; the near-meaning group holds single ornaments and closely related nouns.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jewel 词干；近义组收单件饰物与关系很近的名词。

entries.definition: A precious stone or one ornament set with one.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，指宝石或单件饰物。

entries.definition: A person who makes or sells jewels.
entries.definitionCN: 由 jewel 加 -er 构成，指珠宝商。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same word.
A chain or string worn round the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 指项链，是 jewellery 中的一件。

entries.definition: Anything added for decoration.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指装饰品，范围比 jewellery 大得多。

entries.definition: A small cheap ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 指廉价的小饰物，常含轻视意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin plaything to the safe and the insurance list.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩物」走到保险箱和保单清单。

normal.en: Late Latin jocale came from jocus, a joke or plaything.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 jocale 源自 jocus，意为玩笑、玩物。

normal.en: English took jewel from French jouel.
normal.cn: 英语从法语 jouel 借来 jewel。

normal.en: Jewellery is uncountable, so a piece of jewellery counts it.
normal.cn: jewellery 不可数，用 a piece of jewellery 来计数。

normal.en: British jewellery doubles the l; American jewelry does not.
normal.cn: 英式 jewellery 双写 l，美式 jewelry 不双写。

normal.en: The same stem gives jeweller and bejewelled.
normal.cn: 同一词干还生出 jeweller 与 bejewelled。

abstract.en: Jewellery is a family of small lights kept in one box.
abstract.cn: 首饰是一盒收在一起的许多小光点。

abstract.en: A jewel is one star; jewellery is the whole night sky.
abstract.cn: jewel 是一颗星，jewellery 是整片夜空。

abstract.en: The old word for a plaything became the word for treasure.
abstract.cn: 曾经的「玩物」一词变成了「珍宝」一词。

examples.en: She never travels with her jewellery.
examples.cn: 她从不带着首饰出门。

examples.en: The museum displays jewellery from ancient tombs.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出古墓出土的首饰。

examples.en: Cheap jewellery can still look elegant.
examples.cn: 廉价的首饰也能显得雅致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「久饿而绿」—— 首饰放久了不戴，铜的都会变绿

root: 晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物、饰物」（源自 jocus「玩笑」）→ 古法语 joel、jouel → 英语 jewel → 加 -ery 构成集合名词 jewellery。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the class of ornaments, precious pieces, the trade, cheap imitations, and the collection of one person.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：饰物总称、镶宝首饰、珠宝行业、装饰仿品，以及个人的全部珍藏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small bright objects spread on dark velvet.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色绒布上摊开的小而亮的东西。

branches.en: THE DISH LINE: rings and chains lying together as one group.
branches.cn: 托盘这条线：戒指和链子一起摊成一组。

branches.en: THE SAFE LINE: stones valuable enough to be insured.
branches.cn: 保险箱这条线：值钱到需要上保险的石头。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: the craft that turns stones into a living.
branches.cn: 工坊这条线：把手艺变成生计。

branches.en: THE STAGE: bright imitations worn under the lights.
branches.cn: 舞台这条线：灯光下戴着的亮仿品。

branches.en: THE BOX LINE: what one woman keeps and passes on.
branches.cn: 木盒这条线：一个人收藏并传下去的东西。

intro.en: Jewellery is jewel plus a collective ending; English endings do the visible work here.
intro.cn: jewellery 是 jewel 加集合后缀，这里起作用的主要是英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The deeper relatives descend from late Latin jocale, a plaything.
latinIntro.cn: 更深的同族可追到晚期拉丁语 jocale「玩物」。

items.example: The jewel fell from its setting.
items.exampleCN: 那颗石子从托上掉了下来。
它把 jeweller 变成 jewellery。
英式拼写保留了两个 l。
它把词变成形容词 bejewelled。

items.example: A jewelly shine is a loose description.
items.exampleCN: 有光泽像珠宝是一种随意的描写。

definition_zh: 娱乐的；休闲的；消遣用的
definition_en: relating to recreation; used for leisure; taken for pleasure rather than medical need
core_image: 湖边一排彩色的脚踏船和自行车
scene: 湖边租船处排着一排彩色的脚踏船，孩子们在挑颜色。 The town opened a new recreational area beside the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 recreational 是「休闲的」（第 2 个义项：供休闲使用的）；句意为小镇在湖边新开了一片休闲区。画面里可留意：彩色的脚踏船、挑颜色的孩子。

pos.zh: 娱乐的；休闲的；消遣用的

senses.title: Relating to enjoyable activity
senses.definition: connected with activities done for enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 与为乐趣而做的活动有关
senses.example: Swimming is a recreational sport for most people.
senses.exampleCN: 对大多数人来说，游泳是一项娱乐性运动。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun recreation to whatever serves it, so any game played for fun is recreational.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 recreation 连接到为它服务的事物上，因此任何为乐趣而玩的游戏都是 recreational。

senses.title: Used for leisure
senses.definition: built or set aside for leisure rather than work
senses.definitionCN: 为休闲而非工作而建造或留出的
senses.example: The town opened a new recreational area beside the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇在湖边新开了一片休闲区。
senses.why: A place marked off for pleasure takes the adjective, because its purpose is the restoring of people.
senses.whyCN: 一块为快乐而划出的地方会带上这个形容词，因为它的目的是让人恢复。

senses.title: Taken for pleasure
senses.definition: used for enjoyment rather than for medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为享乐而非治疗而使用
senses.example: The law separates recreational use from medical use.
senses.exampleCN: 法律把消遣性使用与医疗使用区分开来。
senses.why: When a substance is taken for pleasure rather than health, the same adjective marks the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当某种物质是为快乐而非健康而使用时，正是同一个形容词标记出这一区别。

intro.en: Recreational is the noun of leisure with an adjective ending: everything that serves refreshment takes the label.
intro.cn: recreational 是表休闲的名词加形容词词尾：一切为恢复服务的事物都带上这个标签。

items.en: Creare meant to create or produce, the root of the family.
items.cn: creare 意为创造或产生，是词族的词根。

items.en: Recreare meant to restore or refresh a tired body.
items.cn: recreare 意为恢复或使疲惫的身体清新。

items.en: English recreation named both restoration and leisure activity.
items.cn: 英语 recreation 既指恢复，也指休闲活动。

items.en: The suffix -al means relating to, giving recreational.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 意为「与……有关的」，由此构成 recreational。

items.en: Modern English applies the adjective to places, sports, and casual drug use.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个形容词用于场所、运动与消遣性用药。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives with similar endings; the near-meaning group gathers words of leisure and pleasure.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾相似的形容词；近义组收表休闲与乐趣的词。

entries.definition: Good at producing new ideas.
Responding to a stimulus.
Something newly made.
Free time for enjoyment.
Giving enjoyment.
Relaxed and not serious.
Not used as medicine.

normalIntro.en: The word is recreation plus al: anything that serves leisure carries the label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 recreation 加 al：凡为休闲服务的事物，都带上这个标签。

normal.en: Recreation plus -al: relating to leisure.
normal.cn: recreation 加 -al：与休闲有关。

normal.en: A recreational area is land set aside for play.
normal.cn: recreational area 是为玩乐留出的地方。

normal.en: Recreational facilities include pools, courts, and trails.
normal.cn: recreational facilities 包括泳池、球场与步道。

normal.en: The stress stays on the third syllable, as in recreation.
normal.cn: 重音仍在第三音节，与 recreation 一致。

normal.en: Recreational use of a drug means use for pleasure, not treatment.
normal.cn: 药物的 recreational use 指为享乐而非治疗而使用。

abstract.en: A recreational space is a city admitting that people need more than work.
abstract.cn: 休闲空间，是一座城市承认人需要的不仅是工作。

abstract.en: Play labelled recreational is play that society permits itself.
abstract.cn: 被标为休闲的玩乐，是社会允许自己拥有的玩乐。

abstract.en: The adjective turns pleasure into a category of planning.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词把快乐变成了规划中的一个类别。

examples.en: Swimming is a recreational sport for most people.
examples.cn: 对大多数人来说，游泳是一项娱乐性运动。

examples.en: The town opened a new recreational area beside the lake.
examples.cn: 小镇在湖边新开了一片休闲区。

examples.en: The law separates recreational use from medical use.
examples.cn: 法律把消遣性使用与医疗使用区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: recreation（消遣）加 al（……的）：与消遣有关的，就是 recreational——娱乐的、休闲的。

root: recreation（消遣）+ 后缀 -al（……的）→ recreational；recreation 源自拉丁 recreare；同族有 recreationally。

sensesIntro.en: The core is serving refreshment; the senses move from enjoyable activity to leisure places and to pleasure use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为恢复服务」；义项从娱乐活动，到休闲场所，再到消遣性使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bright paddle boats waiting at a lakeside jetty.
core.cn: 核心意象：湖边码头旁排着一排色彩鲜亮的脚踏船。

branches.en: a swimmer in a public pool
branches.cn: 公共泳池里的游泳者

branches.en: a new park by the lake
branches.cn: 湖边新建的公园

branches.en: a pleasure taken without a prescription
branches.cn: 不凭处方取用的享乐

branches.en: a game and a place built for it
branches.cn: 游戏与为它建造的场所

branches.en: a leisure area and a leisure choice
branches.cn: 休闲场所与休闲选择

intro.en: A noun of leisure takes a Latin adjective ending, and the adjective spreads from sports to places to casual use.
intro.cn: 一个表休闲的名词接上拉丁形容词词尾，这个形容词便从运动扩展到场所，再到消遣性使用。

latinIntro.en: The base is recreare, to refresh, and the ending -al marks a relation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 recreare（使恢复），词尾 -al 标记关联。

definition_zh: 毗连的；邻近的；紧接着的；（几何）邻接的
definition_en: next to or very near something, or immediately following it
core_image: 两栋房子共用同一面墙，门牌号只差一号
scene: 旅馆走廊尽头那扇门后，就是我们要找的房间。 Our room is adjacent to the lecture hall.
sceneCN: 这里的 adjacent 是「毗连的」（第 1 个义项：位置紧挨着）；句意是我们的房间紧挨着报告厅。

pos.zh: 形容词：毗连的；邻近的；紧接着的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「邻接；邻近」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「相邻地」

senses.title: Next to in space
senses.definition: lying next to something or sharing a border with it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物旁边，或与它共有一条边界
senses.example: The library is adjacent to the main gate.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆紧挨着正门。
senses.why: Latin adiacere is ad- 'near' plus iacere 'to lie', so the word literally pictures one thing lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adiacere 是 ad-（靠近）加 iacere（躺），字面就是「一物躺在另一物旁边」。

senses.title: Immediately following in order
senses.definition: coming immediately after something in a series, text or process
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列事物、文本或过程中紧接在某物之后
senses.example: The chapter adjacent to this one deals with grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 紧接这一章的那一章讲的是语法。
senses.why: If two things lie side by side on a page or in a list, the second one touches the first; nearness in space becomes nearness in order.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西在纸面或清单上并排躺着，后者就贴着前者；空间上的邻近于是变成顺序上的紧接。

senses.title: Sharing a side or vertex in geometry
senses.definition: describing angles or sides that share a common vertex or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 指角或边共用同一个顶点或边界
senses.example: In the figure, the two adjacent angles add up to a straight angle.
senses.exampleCN: 在图中，这两个邻角相加等于一个平角。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest literal sense: two figures lie against each other along a shared edge.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了最早的字面义：两个图形沿着一条共用的边彼此贴靠。

intro.en: A Latin verb of lying near became an adjective of nearness.
intro.cn: 一个表示「躺在旁边」的拉丁动词，变成了表示邻近的形容词。

items.en: iacere meant to lie down or to throw, and it underlies project and reject as well.
items.cn: iacere 意为躺下或投掷，project 与 reject 也出自这个词。

items.en: ad- 'near' plus iacere formed adiacere, to lie near, with the participle adiacens.
items.cn: ad-（靠近）加 iacere 构成 adiacere「位于附近」，分词为 adiacens。

items.en: The noun adiacentia named neighbourhood, the state of lying next to something.
items.cn: 名词 adiacentia 表示「邻近」，即紧挨着某物的状态。

items.en: English borrowed adjacent in the sixteenth century, mainly in geometry and land surveying.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 adjacent，主要用于几何与土地测量。

items.en: It now covers rooms, plots, fields and stages of a process, always stressing contact or nearness.
items.cn: 如今它可用于房间、地块、田野与流程阶段，始终强调接触或接近。

note.en: The first group shares the lying-near root; the second gathers words for being next to something.
note.cn: 第一组共享「躺在旁边」的词根；第二组是几个表示「紧挨」的词。

entries.definition: the state of being next to something
in a neighbouring position
to be next to or joined with
situated next to another
joined to or touching
lying along a border
a short distance away

normalIntro.en: iacere, to lie, sits inside the -jacent part.
normalIntro.cn: 意为「躺」的 iacere 就藏在 -jacent 这一截里。

normal.en: ad- means near and iacere means to lie: lying near.
normal.cn: ad- 是「靠近」，iacere 是「躺」，合起来是「躺在旁边」。

normal.en: adjacent is almost always followed by to.
normal.cn: adjacent 后面几乎总跟着 to。

normal.en: Two adjacent rooms share a wall and need no hyphen.
normal.cn: adjacent rooms 共用一堵墙，中间不加连字符。

normal.en: The noun adjacency keeps the same c before the y.
normal.cn: 名词 adjacency 在 y 前仍保留了那个 c。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with adjective, which names a word class.
normal.cn: 别和 adjective 混淆，后者是「形容词」这个类别名。

abstract.en: Picture two flat doors whose frames touch.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇公寓门，门框紧碰在一起。

abstract.en: See a row of shops, each one leaning on the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一排店铺，一家靠着另一家。

abstract.en: Think of two facing pages of an open book.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的书里相对的两页。

examples.en: The library is adjacent to the main gate.
examples.cn: 图书馆紧挨着正门。

examples.en: He took the seat adjacent to mine.
examples.cn: 他坐在我旁边的座位上。

examples.en: The two adjacent angles add up to a straight angle.
examples.cn: 这两个邻角相加等于一个平角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿杰森特」——阿杰特别会挑位子，每次都坐在我旁边。

root: 拉丁语 adiacere（位于附近），由 ad-（靠近）与 iacere（躺）构成；字面即「躺在旁边」，后用于空间、顺序与几何。

sensesIntro.en: Lying beside another thing covers rooms, chapters and angles.
sensesIntro.cn: 「躺在另一物旁边」这一画面，管着房间、章节与角。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things lying side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西并排躺着。

branches.en: two rooms sharing one wall
branches.cn: 两个房间共用一堵墙

branches.en: a plot touching the road
branches.cn: 紧贴马路的地块

branches.en: a chapter right after another
branches.cn: 紧接在另一章之后的章节

branches.en: angles sharing one side
branches.cn: 共用一条边的角

branches.en: nearness in space turned into nearness in order
branches.cn: 空间上的邻近转为顺序上的紧接

intro.en: A prefix of nearness plus a Latin verb of lying.
intro.cn: 一个表示「靠近」的词头，加一个表示「躺」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: iacere also underlies project, inject and subject.
latinIntro.cn: iacere 也是 project、inject 与 subject 的词根。

definition_zh: 痕迹；踪迹；微量；（作动词）追溯；追踪；描摹
definition_en: a mark or sign left by something that has passed, or to follow such marks back to their source
core_image: 泥地上的一串脚印，一直延伸到树林里
scene: 雨后的田埂上留着一行野兽的脚印，猎狗低头嗅着，一步一步往里走。 The hunters followed the trace of a deer to the edge of the marsh.
sceneCN: 这里 trace 是「踪迹、痕迹」（第 1 个义项：某物经过后留下的印记）；句意为猎人循着鹿的踪迹一直走到了沼泽边缘。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「描摹；追踪；描图纸」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「追踪者；示踪剂」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可追溯的」

senses.title: A mark left behind by movement
senses.definition: a sign such as footprints, a line, or a stain left by something moving or present
senses.definitionCN: 由物体移动或出现而留下的脚印、线条或污渍等记号
senses.example: There were fresh traces of mud on the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房地板上留下了新鲜的泥痕。
senses.why: The Latin source is a verb of drawing a line, so a trace is what a passing line leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源是「画线」的动词，所以痕迹就是一条经过的线所留下的东西。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a tiny quantity of something, especially one barely detectable
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，尤指几乎难以察觉的一点
senses.example: The water showed traces of copper from the old pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 水里检出了老管道带来的一丝铜。
senses.why: If only a mark remains of something, then only a little of it is left, and that little becomes the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 若某物只剩下一个印记，那就只剩一点点，而这一点点便成了第二个义项。

senses.title: To follow marks to their source
senses.definition: to find the origin or history of something by following the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 循着证据找出某物的起源或来历
senses.example: Scholars traced the proverb back to a Latin writer.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们把这句谚语追溯到一位拉丁作家。
senses.why: Following a line drawn by something is following its path backwards, which is what tracing an origin means.
senses.whyCN: 顺着某物画出的线走，就是反向跟随它的路径，这正是「追溯起源」的意思。

senses.title: To copy a shape by drawing over it
senses.definition: to copy a picture by placing thin paper over it and drawing the lines
senses.definitionCN: 把薄纸覆在图上，照着线条描出图形
senses.example: She traced the outline of the leaf onto the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把叶子的轮廓描到了纸上。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the Latin verb is to draw a line, and copying a shape is the most literal drawing of lines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词最古老的含义就是画线，而照着轮廓画线是最字面的用法。

senses.title: To find the course of something
senses.definition: to follow the path or development of something step by step
senses.definitionCN: 一步一步跟随某物的路线或发展
senses.example: They traced the river from the mountains to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从山间到大海沿途追查这条河。
senses.why: Once you have a line, you can walk along it, and the word moves from drawing a path to following one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了一条线，就能顺着它走，于是这个词从「画路径」转到「跟随路径」。

intro.en: Trace comes from Old French tracier, from Latin tractus, a dragging or a drawing out, which is built on the verb trahere, to pull.
intro.cn: trace 来自古法语 tracier，源自拉丁语 tractus（拖、拉出），建立在动词 trahere（拉）之上。

items.en: Trahere means to pull or draw; its participle tractus means a dragging or a drawn line.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉、拖；其分词 tractus 意为「拖拽」或「画出的线」。

items.en: Old French tracier means to draw a line, to mark out a path, or to make a sketch.
items.cn: 古法语 tracier 意为画线、标出路径或勾勒草图。

items.en: English borrows the word first for a mark on the ground left by a person or animal.
items.cn: 英语先借入这个词，指人或动物留在地上的印记。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the abstract sense of tracing a story or a family back to its origin develops.
items.cn: 十七世纪发展出「把一段经过或一个家族追溯到源头」的抽象含义。

items.en: The scientific use for tiny amounts, such as trace elements, becomes standard in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示极微量的科学用法（如微量元素）在十九、二十世纪成为标准。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin pulling root, while the near-meaning group gathers words for signs and for following a path.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在拉丁语「拉」这一词根上的词，近义组收集表示记号与跟随路径的词。
