something that follows or marks a course
a path or the marks left on it
entries.definitionCN: 轨道；足迹，拼写相近但来源不同

entries.definition: to pull something out
a visible sign on a surface
signs that show something is true
a mark left by a foot

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the pulling root, from the family with -ing, -er, and -able, and from the collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「拉」这个词根、由 -ing、-er、-able 构成的词族以及常用搭配入手。

normal.en: Trahere is to pull, so a trace is something drawn out along a line.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉，所以 trace 是沿着一条线拉出来的东西。

normal.en: Trace, tracing, tracer, traceable: noun, act, person, and possibility.
normal.cn: trace、tracing、tracer、traceable，分别是名词、行为、人、可能性。

normal.en: Trace back to is the key phrase: follow the line backwards until it starts.
normal.cn: trace back to 是关键搭配：沿着线往回走，直到它的起点。

normal.en: Without a trace means the line has disappeared completely.
normal.cn: without a trace 意味着这条线完全消失了。

normal.en: A trace of salt is a mark of salt left in the water, not the salt itself.
normal.cn: a trace of salt 是水里的盐留下的印记，而不是盐本身。

abstract.en: Picture a finger drawing a line in dust, then the line slowly being blown away.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在灰上画出一条线，然后线被慢慢吹散。

abstract.en: Think of a thin thread pulled out of a cloth, going back to the loom.
abstract.cn: 想一根从布里抽出的细线，一路回到织机。

abstract.en: A trace is the past still visible on a surface.
abstract.cn: 痕迹是仍然留在表面上的过去。

examples.en: The police found no trace of the missing boat.
examples.cn: 警方没有找到失踪船只的任何踪迹。

examples.en: The word traces back to an old French verb.
examples.cn: 这个词可以追溯到古法语的一个动词。

examples.en: There was a trace of anger in her voice.
examples.cn: 她的声音里有一丝怒意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戳一斯」——在泥里戳一下，留下一条印子，就是痕迹。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拖）→ 分词 tractus（拉出的线）→ 古法语 tracier（画线）→ 中古英语 trace。同源词有 track、tract、extract、attract、contract。

sensesIntro.en: From the drawn line the entry spreads in two directions: backwards into the mark left behind and the tiny remains it implies, and forwards into drawing copies and following paths to an origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「画出的线」出发，本词向两个方向展开：向内是留下的印记以及由此而来的微量残余，向外是描摹与循路追到源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line in the dust showing where something passed.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰土上的一条线，显示出某物经过的路线。

branches.en: The mark itself.
branches.cn: 印记本身。

branches.en: The little that the mark implies.
branches.cn: 印记所暗示的那一点残余。

branches.en: The line drawn by copying.
branches.cn: 照着描出的线。

branches.en: The line followed along a route.
branches.cn: 沿着路线跟随的线。

branches.en: The line followed back to its start.
branches.cn: 顺着线走回起点。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin stem tract- pulled into French and English, and its family is formed with -ing, -er, and -able.
intro.cn: 本词带着拉丁词干 tract- 经法语进入英语，其词族由 -ing、-er、-able 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb and its participle are the base of the whole English family, from trace to extract.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁动词及其分词是 trace 到 extract 整个英语词族的基础。

items.example: The stem appears in trace, track, and extract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 trace、track、extract 中。

items.example: Tracing is the act and its product.
items.exampleCN: tracing 既是行为也是产物。

items.example: Traceable means it can be followed back.

latinEntries.meaning: drawn; a drawing out, a course

definition_zh: 发起；开始实施；使初步了解；（经仪式）接纳为新成员
definition_en: to cause a process to begin, or to formally introduce someone into a group or skill
core_image: 第一块多米诺骨牌被手指轻轻推倒
scene: 会议室里摊开一叠项目提案，等待签字。 The council voted to initiate a review of the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 initiate 是「发起、开始实施」（第 1 个义项：促使某个过程开始）；句意为议会表决通过，启动对整个体系的审查。图中可辨识物件：提案、签字笔、桌灯。

pos.zh: 动词：发起；开始实施；引导入门；接纳为成员
名词：新加入者（多见于专业书面语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会仪式」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
同根形容词，义为「最初的」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「发起者」

senses.title: To start a process
senses.definition: to make a process, plan, or action begin
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程、计划或行动开始
senses.example: The company initiated a new training programme.
senses.exampleCN: 公司启动了一项新的培训计划。
senses.why: Latin initiare is to begin, from initium "a beginning"; the verb names the act of opening the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initiare 意为「开始」，源自 initium「开端」；动词指的就是把门打开这一动作。

senses.title: To introduce someone to something new
senses.definition: to help someone learn about a subject or activity for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人第一次了解某学科或活动
senses.example: The course initiates students into the basics of law.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课引导学生进入法学的基础领域。
senses.why: To enter a new field is to be led through a beginning, so the verb means both to start and to bring someone to the start.
senses.whyCN: 进入新领域就是被带过一个开端，所以这个动词既表示开始，也表示把人领到起点。

senses.title: To admit someone by ceremony
senses.definition: to formally accept someone into a group, often with a special ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式接纳某人加入团体，常有专门仪式
senses.example: New members are initiated at the spring meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新成员在春季会议上被正式接纳。
senses.why: Secret societies and clubs turned the doorway image into a real rite of passage.
senses.whyCN: 秘密社团与俱乐部把「门」的意象变成了真实的入会仪式。

intro.en: Initiate is the Latin verb of beginning that English borrowed for plans, lessons and ceremonies alike.
intro.cn: initiate 是拉丁语表示「开始」的动词，英语用它兼指计划、入门与仪式。

items.en: Inire, from in- and ire "to go", meant "to go in, to begin".
items.cn: inire 由 in- 与 ire「走」构成，意为「进入、开始」。

items.en: Initium, "a beginning", and the verb initiare, "to begin or admit", followed from it.
items.cn: 由它派生出 initium「开端」以及动词 initiare「开始、接纳」。

items.en: In religious use initiare meant to admit someone to the mysteries, a sacred beginning.
items.cn: 在宗教用法中 initiare 指让人进入秘仪，是一种神圣的开端。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the seventeenth century for starting actions and for formal admission.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用这个动词，用于发起行动与正式纳新。

items.en: Business and law now use it for launching projects and proceedings.
items.cn: 如今商业与法律领域用它表示启动项目与程序。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the root of beginning; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of starting.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示「开始」的动词。

The adjective for what comes first.
The act of starting, or a ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「开始、入会仪式」。

entries.definition: To start something big with publicity, like a product or a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推出、发射」，多指有声势地启动产品或船只。

entries.definition: The most general verb for starting anything.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始」，最通用的说法。

entries.definition: To cause something to happen suddenly, like a reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引发」，强调突然触发反应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb of beginning and the phrases the word routinely takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「开始」动词，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Initium is a beginning: to initiate is to push the first domino.
normal.cn: initium 是开端：initiate 就是推倒第一块骨牌。

normal.en: The noun initiative keeps the same root: the will to begin.
normal.cn: 名词 initiative 同根，指「开始的意愿」。

normal.en: Companies initiate projects, courts initiate proceedings.
normal.cn: 公司发起项目，法院启动程序。

normal.en: Be initiated into a club means to be let in through its door.
normal.cn: be initiated into a club 指被放进俱乐部的大门。

normal.en: An initiator is whoever acts first.
normal.cn: initiator 就是最先行动的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger on the first domino: everything after that is consequence.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按在第一块骨牌上：其后的一切都是后果。

abstract.en: Initiate is a choice, not an accident: someone decides the beginning will happen.
abstract.cn: initiate 是一种选择而非偶然：有人决定让开始发生。

abstract.en: Every beginning costs something, which is why starting is harder than continuing.
abstract.cn: 每个开始都有代价，这正是开始比继续更难的原因。

examples.en: The government initiated talks with the union.
examples.cn: 政府启动了与工会的谈判。

examples.en: Senior students initiate the newcomers into college life.
examples.cn: 高年级学生引导新生适应大学生活。

examples.en: The club initiated ten new members last month.
examples.cn: 俱乐部上个月正式接纳了十名新成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你谁特」——一开始就问你是谁，然后让你入门

root: 拉丁语 inire「走进、开始」（in- + ire「走」）派生 initium「开端」与 initiare「开始、接纳」；英语十七世纪借入 initiate。同根词：initial、initially、initiative、initiation。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all show a doorway being opened: a process begins, a learner is led in, a member is formally admitted.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在展示一扇被打开的门：过程开始、学习者被领进门、成员被正式接纳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tips the first domino and the whole line falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指推倒第一块骨牌，整排随之倒下。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: a plan or policy is initiated when someone starts it.
branches.cn: 项目这条线：方案或政策在有人启动它时被 initiate。

branches.en: THE COURT: legal action is initiated by the party who files first.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：诉讼由先提起诉讼的一方 initiate。

branches.en: THE LESSON: a teacher initiates beginners into a subject.
branches.cn: 课堂这条线：老师把初学者领进一门学科。

branches.en: THE RITE: a club initiates new members with a ceremony.
branches.cn: 仪式这条线：俱乐部用仪式接纳新成员。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense puts someone or something on the inside of a beginning.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都把人或事放到了开端的里面。

intro.en: Initiate is the Latin verb of beginning, keeping its Latin verb ending in English.
intro.cn: initiate 是拉丁语「开始」动词，英语保留了它的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire, initium and initiare are recorded, all built on the verb ire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inire、initium、initiare 均有记录，都建立在动词 ire 上。

items.example: It marks entering the new state.
The base of the whole family.

items.exampleCN: 这是 initiate 的直接来源。

items.example: It carries the Latin verb ending into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁动词词尾带进英语。

definition_zh: 无论哪一个；随便哪一个；（从句）…的任何一项
definition_en: used to say that any one of a set will do, or to introduce a clause naming any member without saying which
core_image: 一整排门都被推开，随便进哪一扇都通向同一个院子
scene: 院子里一圈门全都敞着，无论走进哪一扇，最后都到同一个天井。 Take whichever seat you like.
sceneCN: 这里 whichever 是「无论哪一个」（第 1 个义项：集合里随便哪一个都行）；句意为你想坐哪个座位都行。整排门全敞着、进哪扇都到同一个院子的画面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 无论哪一个；随便哪一个

senses.title: Any one will do
senses.definition: used to say that no member of a set is excluded and any choice is acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 表示集合中没有任何成员被排除，任何选择都可以
senses.example: Take whichever seat you like.
senses.exampleCN: 你想坐哪个座位都行。
senses.why: Adding ever to which removes the narrowing: every member of the set is now allowed.
senses.whyCN: 在 which 后面加 ever 就取消了收窄，集合里每个成员都被允许。

senses.title: No matter which
senses.titleCN: 无论哪一个（都不改变结果）
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause saying the result stays the same whichever member is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个从句，表示无论选哪一个，结果都不变
senses.example: Whichever road you take, the drive lasts an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 无论你走哪条路，车程都有一小时。
senses.why: The same total coverage also works as a concession, since the outcome does not depend on the pick.
senses.whyCN: 同样的全覆盖也能作让步，因为结果并不取决于挑哪一个。

senses.title: The one that turns up
senses.definition: used as a pronoun to mean any member of the set that fits the description
senses.definitionCN: 作代词使用，指集合中符合描述的任何一项
senses.example: Whichever of the two finishes first will report to me.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个谁先做完，就向我汇报。
senses.why: Because no member is fixed, the word must be able to stand as the subject of its own clause.
senses.whyCN: 因为没有固定成员，这个词就必须能充当自己从句的主语。

intro.en: Whichever is which plus the old emphatic ever, a combination that spread in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
intro.cn: whichever 是 which 加上古老的强调词 ever，这种组合在十五、十六世纪流行起来。

items.en: Hwylc was the simple word for which, with no widening at all.
items.cn: hwylc 只是单纯的「哪一个」，完全没有放宽。

items.en: The form ǣfre, meaning at any time, began to attach to question words.
items.cn: 意为「任何时候」的 ǣfre 开始黏附在疑问词上。

items.en: Whichever settled in print next to whatever and whoever, completing the set.
items.cn: whichever 与 whatever、whoever 一起固定进书面语，凑齐了这一组。

items.en: Grammar keeps whichever for a closed set and whatever for an open one.
items.cn: 语法上 whichever 用于封闭的集合，whatever 用于开放的范围。

items.en: In careful writing whichever is preferred for a choice among named things.
items.cn: 在严谨写作中，在已点明的事物之间做选择时更偏好 whichever。

note.en: The first group is the ever family, the second the words that also say it does not matter which.
note.cn: 第一组是 ever 家族，第二组是同样表示「哪个都无所谓」的说法。

entries.definition: The same word without the widening.
The ever form for an open set.
The ever form for people.
The same word plus way, a very common spoken pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 无论哪个方式（口语常用）

entries.definition: One or the other of just two.
One at random from an open group.
The person version of any one.
Whatever the route, a concession in three words.

normalIntro.en: Which asks the member; ever says the answer does not matter, so the two together cover the whole set.
normalIntro.cn: which 问成员是谁，ever 说答案无所谓，两者合起来就覆盖整个集合。

normal.en: Whichever works only inside a known list, so keep the list in view.
normal.cn: whichever 只在已知的名单里工作，所以要一直看着名单。

normal.en: Whichever for a closed set, whatever for an open one.
normal.cn: 封闭集合用 whichever，开放范围用 whatever。

normal.en: The stress falls on ev, and that stressed ever is the whole meaning.
normal.cn: 重音落在 ev 上，那个加重的 ever 就是全部意义。

normal.en: Swallowed whole, it often sounds like which-ever with a tiny pause.
normal.cn: 整块吞下去念，听起来像 which-ever，中间带一点停顿。

normal.en: Whichever comes first is the everyday English for this word.
normal.cn: whichever comes first 是这个词最日常的说法。

abstract.en: See every door standing open at once.
abstract.cn: 想所有门同时敞开。

abstract.en: Hear a shrug inside one word.
abstract.cn: 听一个词里藏着一次耸肩。

abstract.en: Feel the freedom of a choice that cannot go wrong.
abstract.cn: 感受一种怎样都不会错的选择自由。

examples.en: Choose whichever colour you prefer.
examples.cn: 你喜欢哪种颜色就选哪种。

examples.en: Whichever team wins, the final will be close.
examples.cn: 无论哪队赢，决赛都会很接近。

examples.en: Whichever of them calls first, tell me at once.
examples.cn: 他们谁先打来，立刻告诉我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为其饿」——为它饿着等：哪个先来就吃哪个，无论哪个都行。

root: which + ever（古英语 ǣfre，任何时候）→ whichever；同族有 whatever、whoever、whenever。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as which with the narrowing removed, becomes a concession when the result does not change, and finally stands alone as a pronoun.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词由取消收窄的 which 而来，在结果不变时成为让步，最后又能单独作代词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of doors all open on the same courtyard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排门全敞着，通向同一个院子。

branches.en: The permission branch: take whichever seat you like.
branches.cn: 许可分支：想坐哪个座位都行。

branches.en: The concession branch: whichever road you take.
branches.cn: 让步分支：无论走哪条路。

branches.en: The subject branch: whichever finishes first reports to me.
branches.cn: 主语分支：谁先做完就向我汇报。

branches.en: The closed-set branch: only among known things.
branches.cn: 封闭集合分支：只在已知事物之间。

branches.en: The stress branch: the ever carries the accent.
branches.cn: 重音分支：ever 部分承载重音。

intro.en: Whichever is easy to take apart: the question word plus the old free-standing ever.
intro.cn: whichever 很好拆：疑问词加上古老而可独立使用的 ever。

latinIntro.en: Latin formed the same idea with quicumque, one word that already contains the total sense; the entries below are counterparts, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quicumque 一个词就表达了同样的全覆盖之意；下面的条目是对应形式，并非来源。

items.example: It makes a concession in three words.
It is the everyday spoken pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这是最日常的口语模式。

latinEntries.meaning: whichever of the two you please

definition_zh: 密集的；浓密的；晦涩的
definition_en: with parts packed closely together, thick enough to block light, or hard to read
core_image: 一片树冠层层叠叠，阳光只能漏下几小点
scene: 走进林子深处，枝叶在头顶合拢，光只剩下细碎的斑点。 The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 dense 指「浓密的」（第 1 个义项：东西紧密挤在一起）；句意是浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。

senses.title: Packed closely together
senses.definition: with parts or people close together and little space between
senses.definitionCN: 各部分或人挨得很近、间隙很小的
senses.example: A dense crowd filled the square before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午之前，密集的人群站满了广场。
senses.why: Dense means the space between things has almost disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 密集就是说东西之间的空隙几乎消失了。

senses.title: Thick and hard to see through
senses.definition: so thick that light or sight cannot pass easily
senses.definitionCN: 厚到光线或视线难以穿过的
senses.example: The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。
senses.why: When branches close over your head, the sky becomes a rumour.
senses.whyCN: 枝叶在头顶合拢时，天空就只剩一个传闻。

senses.title: Hard to read or follow
senses.definition: written in words so packed that it is hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 文字过于密集而难以读懂的
senses.example: The report was dense with figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告塞满数字，读起来很吃力。
senses.why: When ideas stand shoulder to shoulder, a reader has no room to walk.
senses.whyCN: 念头肩并肩站着时，读者就没有走动的余地。

intro.en: Dense comes straight from Latin densus, meaning thick or crowded, and has kept that shape for centuries.
intro.cn: dense 直接来自拉丁语 densus，意为浓密、拥挤，几个世纪以来形状几乎没变。

items.en: Densus described a thick wood or a crowded rank of soldiers.
items.cn: densus 形容茂密的树林或挤紧的士兵队列。

items.en: Writers used it for fog, hair and anything tightly packed.
items.cn: 作家用它写雾、写头发，也写任何紧密挤在一起的东西。

items.en: English borrowed dense for air, smoke and solid matter.
items.cn: 英语借来 dense，用来写空气、烟与固体。

items.en: Science gave it the precise sense of mass in a space.
items.cn: 科学给了它「单位空间里的质量」这一精确含义。

items.en: It now also describes prose that is packed too tightly to enjoy.
items.cn: 如今它也形容塞得太满、读起来不轻松的散文。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dens- stem, and the meaning group gives three ways of being tightly packed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dens- 词干，近义组则给出三种「紧密挤在一起」的说法。

entries.definition: the amount packed into a space
in a closely packed way
to make something smaller or thicker
having a large distance between two sides
full of people or things
pressed into a small space

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with leaves closing over a path and end with a page that gives the eye no rest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从合拢在小路上方的树叶开始，落到一页让眼睛歇不下来的文字。

normal.en: In a dense wood the sky comes to you in pieces.
normal.cn: 在茂密的林子里，天空是一小块一小块来的。

normal.en: Dense fog makes a familiar street into a stranger.
normal.cn: 浓雾能把熟悉的街道变成陌生人。

normal.en: A dense page is a crowd of words with no room to breathe.
normal.cn: 晦涩的一页，是一群没有喘息空间的词。

normal.en: Dense and density differ by a single ending.
normal.cn: dense 与 density 只差一个词尾。

normal.en: Condense is dense with con-, meaning together.
normal.cn: condense 就是 dense 前面加了表示「一起」的 con-。

abstract.en: Picture tree tops touching until the light is only dots.
abstract.cn: 想象树冠彼此相接，光只剩下一粒粒小点。

abstract.en: Picture a bus so full that the door cannot close.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆挤到车门都关不上的公交车。

abstract.en: Picture a paragraph with no white space left.
abstract.cn: 想象一段文字，连一点空白都没剩下。

examples.en: The dense forest kept the midday sun off the ground.
examples.cn: 浓密的森林把正午阳光挡在地面之外。

examples.en: A dense crowd filled the square before noon.
examples.cn: 正午之前，密集的人群站满了广场。

examples.en: The report was dense with figures.
examples.cn: 这份报告塞满数字，读起来很吃力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dense 记成「凳子挤」：想象一排凳子紧紧挨着，中间连脚都插不进去，这就是密集的。

root: 直接来自拉丁语 densus，本义是浓密、拥挤，可形容树林、雾气和挤紧的队列。进入英语后先写空气与固体，十七世纪科学又给了它「单位空间里的质量」这一含义，现代还用它形容过于密集的文字。

sensesIntro.en: From branches closing overhead, to bodies filling a square, to words filling a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头顶合拢的枝叶，到站满广场的人，再到塞满一页的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaves touching until only dots of light get through.
core.cn: 核心意象：树叶彼此相触，只漏下几点光。

branches.en: The first sense is simple crowding, with no gaps left.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是拥挤，空隙被挤没了。

branches.en: The second sense is thickness that blocks light and sight.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是挡住光线与视线的厚度。

branches.en: The third sense is writing packed until reading becomes work.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是挤到阅读变成体力活的文字。

branches.en: A crowd and a fog both fill space until nothing else fits.
branches.cn: 人群与浓雾都填满空间，直到再塞不进别的。

branches.en: Thick fog and thick prose both leave the reader guessing.
branches.cn: 浓雾与晦涩的文字，都让读者只能猜。

intro.en: Dense has a small Latin family: a noun of measure, an adverb of manner and verbs of pressing together.
intro.cn: dense 有一小族拉丁亲戚：表度量的名词、表方式副词，以及表示压紧的动词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin densus, thick or crowded; con- adds the idea of bringing things together.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 densus（浓密、拥挤），前缀 con- 加上「聚到一起」的意思。

items.example: The fog grew dense near the river.

items.meaning: the amount packed into a space
items.example: They measured the density of the liquid.
items.exampleCN: 他们测量了这种液体的密度。

items.example: The denseness of the crowd slowed us.
items.exampleCN: 人群的稠密让我们走得很慢。

items.meaning: to press together or turn to liquid
items.example: Steam condenses on the cold glass.

items.meaning: a device that turns gas into liquid
the change from gas to liquid

items.example: They densified the soil before building.
items.exampleCN: 他们建房前把土压得更实。

definition_zh: 疲劳；劳累；使疲劳；金属疲劳
definition_en: extreme tiredness, the act of making someone tired, or the weakening of metal under repeated stress
core_image: 深夜的办公室里，他揉着眼睛站起来，桌上的咖啡杯已经空了好几次
scene: 连续加班好几天后，他坐在椅子上连手都抬不起来。 Fatigue made every step feel heavy.
sceneCN: 这里 fatigue 是「疲劳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：疲劳让每一步都变得沉重。

senses.title: Extreme tiredness
senses.definition: a state of being extremely tired in body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 身体或精神极度疲惫的状态
senses.example: The long march left the soldiers in deep fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军让士兵们疲惫不堪。
senses.why: This is the central everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词最核心的日常含义。

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to cause a person or body to become extremely tired
senses.definitionCN: 使人或身体变得极度疲惫
senses.example: The night shift fatigues workers quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班很快就会让工人疲惫。
senses.why: The noun sense turns into a verb of causing tiredness.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示「使人疲倦」的动词。

senses.title: Weakness in metal
senses.definition: the weakening of metal caused by repeated stress
senses.definitionCN: 金属因反复受力而变弱的现象
senses.example: Engineers checked the wing for metal fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查机翼是否有金属疲劳。
senses.why: The idea of tiredness is applied to materials under stress.
senses.whyCN: 把「疲劳」的观念用于承受压力的材料。

senses.title: A duty or chore
senses.definition: a task or duty, especially an unpleasant military one
senses.definitionCN: 任务或勤务，尤指军中杂役
senses.example: He was put on kitchen fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 他被派去厨房做杂役。
senses.why: A separate military sense names tiring routine work.
senses.whyCN: 另一个军事义项指令人劳累的日常杂务。

intro.en: Fatigue came into English from French, ultimately from the Latin verb fatigare, to tire out.
intro.cn: fatigue 经法语进入英语，最终源自拉丁语动词 fatigare（使疲惫）。

items.en: Fatigare meant to tire out or wear down.
items.cn: fatigare 意为使筋疲力尽或消耗。

items.en: The noun fatigue named weariness and hard labor.
items.cn: 古法语名词 fatigue 表示疲倦与苦役。

items.en: Fatigue entered English as a word for extreme weariness.
items.cn: fatigue 以「极度疲倦」之义进入英语。

items.en: Military writers used fatigue for tiring routine duties.
items.cn: 军事作家用 fatigue 指令人疲劳的日常勤务。

items.en: Engineers borrowed the word for weakness in stressed metal.
items.cn: 工程师借这个词表示受应力金属的弱化。

note.en: Fatigue is compared with similar-looking words and with words for tiredness.
note.cn: 把 fatigue 与形近词以及表示疲倦的词作比较。

entries.definition: not clear or exact
a secret plan or plot
a death caused by an accident or disaster
the state of being tired
extreme loss of energy
the feeling of being very tired

normalIntro.en: Fatigue is deep tiredness, and the same word describes tired metal.
normalIntro.cn: fatigue 是极度疲惫，同一个词也用来描述金属的疲劳。

normal.en: Fatigue is stronger than ordinary tiredness.
normal.cn: fatigue 比普通的 tiredness 程度更重。

normal.en: Metal fatigue names cracks caused by repeated stress.
normal.cn: metal fatigue 指反复受力造成的裂纹。

normal.en: The verb fatigue means to wear someone out.
normal.cn: 动词 fatigue 意为使某人筋疲力尽。

normal.en: Indefatigable means never getting tired.
normal.cn: indefatigable 意为不知疲倦的。

normal.en: Fatigue duty is tiring routine work.
normal.cn: fatigue duty 指令人劳累的杂务。

abstract.en: Tiredness of the body became a way to describe tiredness of metal.
abstract.cn: 身体的疲惫被用来描述金属的疲劳。

abstract.en: Hard labor links the senses of weariness and duty.
abstract.cn: 艰苦劳作把疲惫与勤务两个义项联系起来。

abstract.en: A word for exhaustion can also name what causes it.
abstract.cn: 表示疲惫的词也可以指造成疲惫的事物。

examples.en: The heat and long hours brought on fatigue.
examples.cn: 炎热和长时间工作引发了疲劳。

examples.en: The steep climb fatigued even the strongest hikers.
examples.cn: 陡峭的山路让最强壮的徒步者都疲惫不堪。

examples.en: Metal fatigue can cause sudden cracks in a bridge.
examples.cn: 金属疲劳可能使桥梁突然开裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: fatigue 源自拉丁语 fatigare（使疲惫），经法语 fatigue 进入英语，含义从「劳作过度」扩展到「金属疲劳」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fatigare（使疲惫），经法语 fatigue 传入，核心义「因过度劳累而衰弱」。

sensesIntro.en: Fatigue means extreme tiredness, the act of tiring someone, weakness in metal, or a tiring duty.
sensesIntro.cn: fatigue 意为极度疲劳、使人疲惫、金属疲劳，或令人劳累的勤务。

core.en: A heavy loss of energy caused by long or hard effort.
core.cn: 因长期或艰苦付出而造成的精力严重损耗。

branches.en: The state of being extremely tired.
branches.cn: 极度疲惫的状态。

branches.en: The act of making someone tired.
branches.cn: 使人疲惫的行为。

branches.en: Weakness caused by stress in metal.
branches.cn: 金属受应力后产生的弱化。

branches.en: A tiring routine duty.
branches.cn: 令人劳累的日常勤务。

branches.en: Feeling tired and causing tiredness are two sides of one process.
branches.cn: 感到疲惫与使人疲惫是同一过程的两个方面。

intro.en: Fatigue builds words for tiredness, for resistance to tiredness, and for extreme weariness.
intro.cn: fatigue 构成表示疲惫、抗疲劳与极度劳累的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fatigare and its noun fatigatio supply the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fatigare 及其名词 fatigatio 提供历史词根。

items.meaning: extreme tiredness or to tire out

items.example: The crew looked fatigued after the flight.
items.exampleCN: 机组人员在飞行后显得很疲惫。

items.example: It was a fatiguing day of travel.
items.exampleCN: 那是令人疲惫的一天旅途。

items.example: Long training can overfatigue young players.
items.exampleCN: 长时间训练会使年轻球员过度疲劳。

items.example: The mat has an antifatigue surface.
items.exampleCN: 这块垫子有抗疲劳表面。
她是一位不知疲倦的研究者。

items.example: He worked indefatigably on the project.
items.exampleCN: 他不知疲倦地投入这个项目。

latinEntries.meaning: to tire out or wear down

latinEntries.example: Fatigatio names a state of weariness.

definition_zh: 鼓励；激励；起鼓励作用的事物
definition_en: the act of giving someone confidence, or something that gives hope
core_image: 一张写着「再试一次」的小纸条，被悄悄塞进课本
scene: 掌声给了她继续表演的鼓励。 The applause gave her encouragement to continue.
sceneCN: 这里 encouragement 是「鼓励」（第 1 个义项：给予信心和支持的行为）；句意：掌声给了她继续表演的鼓励。

senses.title: The act of giving confidence
senses.definition: the act of giving someone support, hope, or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人支持、希望或信心的行为
senses.example: Her encouragement helped me finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她的鼓励帮我跑完了比赛。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb gives, so encouragement is support passed from one person to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词所给予的东西，因此鼓励是从一个人传给另一个人的支持。

senses.title: Something that gives hope
senses.definition: a word, action, or event that makes someone feel more hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到更有希望的言语、行动或事件
senses.example: The letter was a great encouragement.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信是极大的鼓励。
senses.why: Support can be counted as a thing, so a kind message becomes an encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 支持可以被当作具体事物来计数，因此一句善意的话就成了一份鼓励。

intro.en: Encouragement is encourage plus -ment, naming the support that is given.
intro.cn: encouragement 是 encourage 加 -ment，命名所给予的支持。

items.en: Cor, heart, is the root of courage.
items.cn: cor（心）是 courage 的词根。

items.en: Encoragier means to put courage into someone.
items.cn: encoragier 意为把勇气放进某人心里。

items.en: Encourage enters English as a verb.
items.cn: encourage 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The noun encouragement appears for the support given.
items.cn: 名词 encouragement 出现，指给予的支持。

items.en: The word covers both the act and the thing that inspires.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词既指行为，也指鼓舞人的事物。

note.en: Encouragement is support that builds confidence; motivation supplies a reason, and inspiration stirs ideas.
note.cn: encouragement 是建立信心的支持，motivation 提供理由，inspiration 激发想法。

entries.definition: to give someone confidence
giving hope or confidence
given confidence
help given to someone
a reason or drive to act
a sudden good idea or strong feeling

normalIntro.en: Encouragement is courage handed over in words or actions.
normalIntro.cn: encouragement 是用言语或行动递过去的勇气。

normal.en: Words of encouragement help a friend.
normal.cn: 鼓励的话帮助朋友。

normal.en: The coach gave us encouragement.
normal.cn: 教练给了我们鼓励。

normal.en: Her letter was a great encouragement.
normal.cn: 她的信是很大的鼓励。

normal.en: Encouragement builds confidence.
normal.cn: 鼓励建立信心。

normal.en: Encouraging news lifts the team.
normal.cn: 令人鼓舞的消息提升士气。

abstract.en: Picture applause rising after a nervous performance.
abstract.cn: 想象紧张演出后响起的掌声。

abstract.en: See a note tucked inside a textbook.
abstract.cn: 想象夹在课本里的小纸条。

abstract.en: Think of a hand steadying a bicycle.
abstract.cn: 想象扶稳自行车的那只手。

examples.en: Her encouragement helped me finish the race.
examples.cn: 她的鼓励帮我跑完了比赛。

examples.en: The letter was a great encouragement.
examples.cn: 那封信是极大的鼓励。

examples.en: Words of encouragement cost nothing.
examples.cn: 鼓励的话不需要花一分钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因卡瑞吉门特」——把勇气送进别人心里的那份礼物；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: encourage 加名词词尾 -ment，深层词根源自拉丁语 cor（心）。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the act of supporting someone and the message or event that gives hope.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词命名支持他人的行为，以及带来希望的讯息或事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: courage handed over like a small gift.
core.cn: 核心意象：像小礼物一样被递过去的勇气。

branches.en: The base sense is the act of giving support.
branches.cn: 基本义是给予支持的行为。

branches.en: The support can be counted as a message or event.
branches.cn: 这种支持可以具体化为讯息或事件。

branches.en: Act and object both produce confidence.
branches.cn: 行为与事物都产生信心。

branches.en: The -ment ending turns the action into a noun.
branches.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动作变成名词。

branches.en: A single kind word can outweigh a long speech.
branches.cn: 一句善意的话可能胜过长篇讲话。

intro.en: Encouragement is en- plus courage plus -ment, the noun of the whole act.
intro.cn: encouragement 是 en- 加 courage 再加 -ment，是整个行为的名词形式。

latinIntro.en: Courage comes from Latin cor, heart, through Old French corage.
latinIntro.cn: courage 经古法语 corage 来自拉丁语 cor（心）。

items.example: The prefix en- puts courage in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 把勇气放入。

items.example: Courage is the core of encouragement.
items.exampleCN: courage 是 encouragement 的核心。
受鼓励的孩子会再试一次。
令人鼓舞的是，队伍赢了。

definition_zh: 充足的；富裕的；宽敞的；丰满的
definition_en: more than enough in quantity or size, or spacious and roomy
core_image: 一只大篮子，里面装的东西还空着一半
scene: 仓库堆满货箱，取用空间还有很多。 There is ample room for everyone to sit.
sceneCN: 这里 ample 是「充足的」（第 1 个义项：数量上足够甚至有余）；句意为有足够的空间让每个人坐下。

pos.zh: 形容词：充足的；富裕的；宽敞的；丰满的

derivatives.zh: 由 ample 加 -ly 构成，义为「充分地；绰绰有余地」
同源名词，义为「幅度；振幅；广阔」
同源动词，义为「放大；增强；详述」
由 amplify 加 -ication 构成，义为「放大；扩充」
由 amplify 加 -er 构成，义为「放大器」

senses.title: More than enough
senses.definition: enough or more than enough for a particular need
senses.definitionCN: 对某项需要来说足够甚至有余
senses.example: There is ample time to finish the work before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑前有充足的时间完成这项工作。
senses.why: Latin amplus meant 'large, spacious'; a large container holds more than the need, and the word became 'more than enough'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 amplus 意为「大的、宽敞的」；一个大的容器装得比所需更多，于是这个词变成「绰绰有余」。

senses.title: Spacious and roomy
senses.definition: large in size or area, with plenty of space
senses.definitionCN: 面积或体积大，空间充裕
senses.example: The house has an ample garden behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子后面有一座宽敞的花园。
senses.why: The physical sense is the oldest: ample space is simply space that is large enough to move in freely.
senses.whyCN: 物理义最古老：ample 的空间就是大到可以自由走动的空间。

senses.title: Generously full in shape
senses.definition: used of a body or garment that is large and generously proportioned
senses.definitionCN: 形容身体或衣物宽大、比例丰盈
senses.example: The coat was cut in an ample style that suited him.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套剪裁宽大，很适合他。
senses.why: If large size can describe space, it can also describe a body or a garment that fills that space generously.
senses.whyCN: 如果「大」可以形容空间，它也可以形容一个宽裕地占满空间的身体或衣物。

intro.en: Ample comes from a Latin adjective for largeness, and the whole family is about making something bigger.
intro.cn: ample 来自拉丁语中表示「大」的形容词，整个词族都与「使变大」有关。

items.en: Amplus meant 'large, spacious, abundant', and it also gave amplus-based words such as amplitude.
items.cn: amplus 意为「大的、宽敞的、丰富的」，还给出了 amplitude 等词。

items.en: Amplificare meant 'to enlarge, widen', the verb behind amplify.
items.cn: amplificare 意为「扩大、加宽」，是 amplify 背后的动词。

items.en: French ample carried the adjective into English with the sense of plentiful and roomy.
items.cn: 法语 ample 把这个形容词带入英语，含义是充足与宽敞。

items.en: English ample is recorded in the fifteenth century for space and for quantity.
items.cn: 英语 ample 在十五世纪有记录，既用于空间，也用于数量。

items.en: The word now covers time, evidence, opportunity and generous proportions.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖时间、证据、机会以及宽大的体型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin largeness family; the near-meaning group gathers sufficiency words.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「大」词族；近义组收「充足」类词。

entries.definition: To make sound, signal, or an account larger.
entries.definitionCN: 指放大声音、信号或把叙述扩充。

entries.definition: The size of a wave's swing or the breadth of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指波摆动的幅度或某物的广阔。

entries.definition: In a more than sufficient way.
Existing in large amounts.
Just enough for a purpose, with no surplus.
Having a lot of room inside.
Larger or more giving than expected.
entries.definitionCN: 指比预期更大或更慷慨。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a large basket that still has room, then move the largeness to time and shape.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只还有空余的大篮子开始，再把「大」移到时间与体形上。

normal.en: Ample is a big basket: what you need fits with room to spare.
normal.cn: ample 就是一只大篮子：所需的东西装得下，还留有余地。

normal.en: Ample time means the day is a big basket.
normal.cn: ample time 意为这一整天就是一只大篮子。

normal.en: Ample room means the walls are far apart.
normal.cn: ample room 意为墙与墙隔得很远。

normal.en: Amply means with plenty left over.
normal.cn: amply 意为还剩下许多。

normal.en: Amplify makes the same largeness audible.
normal.cn: amplify 让同一种「大」变得可听见。

abstract.en: Picture a market basket filled only halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只装了一半的菜篮。

abstract.en: Now picture the empty half becoming hours on a clock.
abstract.cn: 再想象空着的那一半变成钟上的小时。

abstract.en: The spare half is ample, in space or in time.
abstract.cn: 空出的那一半就是 ample，无论在空间还是时间上。

examples.en: We had ample warning before the storm arrived.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，我们得到了充分的警告。

examples.en: The hall is ample enough for two hundred people.
examples.cn: 这个大厅宽敞得足以容纳两百人。

examples.en: The report offers ample evidence for its claim.
examples.cn: 这份报告为其主张提供了充分的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安普尔」——安，普尔，篮子大得装不满，绰绰有余

root: 拉丁语 amplus（大的、宽敞的、丰富的），经法语 ample 进入英语；核心是「容量大于所需」，由空间义扩展出「充足」与「宽大」义。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one large container: enough and to spare, wide open space, and a body that fills space generously.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享同一个大容器：够用且有余、开阔的空间，以及宽裕地占满空间的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large basket is only half full, with plenty of room left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只大篮子只装了一半，还留着许多空间。

branches.en: THE SURPLUS: the first sense is capacity beyond the need.
branches.cn: 余量线：第一个义项是超出需要的容量。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the second sense is physical space that is wide open.
branches.cn: 空间线：第二个义项是开阔的物理空间。

branches.en: THE BODY: the third sense applies largeness to shape and clothing.
branches.cn: 体形线：第三个义项把「大」用于体形与衣物。

branches.en: THE BASKET: quantity and space are both measured by capacity.
branches.cn: 篮子线：数量与空间都靠容量来衡量。

branches.en: THE PROPORTION: wide space and full shape share the same generosity.
branches.cn: 比例线：开阔的空间与丰满的体形共享同一种宽裕。

intro.en: Ample is a Latin adjective with a productive family of adverbs, nouns and verbs.
intro.cn: ample 是拉丁形容词，拥有能产的副词、名词与动词词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin amplus and the verb amplificare stand behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 amplus 与动词 amplificare 站在词族背后。

items.example: The wave has a large amplitude.

items.meaning: a device that strengthens a signal

items.example: There is ample room in the hall.

definition_zh: 节约的；节省的；经济实惠的；简洁的
definition_en: using money, fuel, time or words carefully without waste, or cheap to buy and run
core_image: 厨房的灯泡换成低瓦数，水龙头也装了限流器
scene: 厨房的灯泡换成低瓦数，水龙头也装了限流器。 This small car is economical to run.
sceneCN: 这里 economical 是「经济实惠的、使用成本低的」（第 2 个义项：运行或使用便宜）；句意为这辆小车用起来很省钱。图中可辨识物件：低瓦数灯泡、限流器、小车。

pos.zh: 形容词：节约的；节省的；经济实惠的；简洁的

collocations.zh: 对真相有所保留（委婉说法）

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「节约地；在经济上」
与本词同源，义为「节约；节省开支」
由否定前缀与本词构成，义为「不节约的；不划算的」

senses.title: Careful with money and resources
senses.titleCN: 节约的：不浪费钱财与资源
senses.definition: using money, fuel, time or materials carefully so that nothing is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎使用金钱、燃料、时间或材料，不让任何东西被浪费
senses.example: The household is economical with water in dry summers.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱的夏天里，这家人很节约用水。
senses.why: The Greek root meant managing a household; the adjective describes a person who manages without waste.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「管理家户」，这个形容词描述的是不浪费地管理的人。

senses.title: Cheap to buy and run
senses.titleCN: 经济实惠的：购买与使用成本低
senses.definition: designed to need little fuel, money or effort to operate
senses.definitionCN: 设计上只需很少燃料、金钱或精力即可运转
senses.example: This small car is economical to run.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆小车用起来很省钱。
senses.why: A machine that manages its fuel like a careful household manager is economical, even though it never holds a purse.
senses.whyCN: 一台像精打细算的当家人那样管理燃料的机器就是 economical，尽管它从不拿钱包。

senses.title: Brief and not wasteful in expression
senses.titleCN: 简洁的：表达不浪费字句
senses.definition: using only the words or means needed, with nothing extra
senses.definitionCN: 只使用所需的字句或手段，没有多余部分
senses.example: Her economical prose leaves no sentence to cut.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文风简洁，没有一句是可以删的。
senses.why: Words are a resource too, so the same habit of not wasting applies to language.
senses.whyCN: 字句也是一种资源，于是「不浪费」的同一习惯也用到了语言上。

intro.en: Economical shares the Greek root of economic but took a different suffix and a narrower everyday sense.
intro.cn: economical 与 economic 共享希腊词根，但取了不同后缀，日常含义也更窄。

items.en: Oikonomikos meant skilled in household management, which is the sense the English adjective first carried.
items.cn: oikonomikos 意为擅长家务管理，这正是英语形容词最早承载的意思。

items.en: The Latin adjective passed into learned European use and later into English.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词进入欧洲的书面语，后来进入英语。

items.en: Economical is recorded in the sixteenth century with the sense of managing a household well.
items.cn: economical 在十六世纪有记录，义为善于管理家户。

items.en: As machines spread, the adjective came to describe engines and lamps that used little fuel.
items.cn: 随着机器普及，这个形容词开始描述耗油少的发动机与省电的灯。

items.en: Economic took the large public sense, leaving economical with personal thrift, low running costs and spare prose.
items.cn: economic 拿走了大型公共义，把个人节俭、低运行成本与简洁文风留给 economical。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pair most often confused; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for thrift and low cost.
note.cn: 形近组收最常被混淆的那一对词；近义组收表示节俭与低成本的形容词。

entries.definition: An adjective for the economy or economics, not for personal thrift.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指经济或经济学，而非个人节俭。

entries.definition: The system of money and trade, or careful use of resources.
entries.definitionCN: 金钱与贸易体系，或对资源的谨慎使用。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning thriftily, or with respect to the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「节约地」，或「在经济方面」。

entries.definition: Careful with money, saving rather than spending.
entries.definitionCN: 用钱谨慎，宁可存下也不乱花。

entries.definition: Simple and cheap, avoiding unnecessary expense.
entries.definitionCN: 简朴而便宜，避免不必要的开支。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow a careful household manager into a low-fuel engine and then into a short sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着一位精打细算的当家人，走进低耗油的发动机，再走进一个短句。

normal.en: Economical is the household word, economic is the national one.
normal.cn: economical 是家户的词，economic 是国家的词。

normal.en: A low-watt bulb and a flow limiter are economical made visible.
normal.cn: 低瓦数灯泡与限流器，就是看得见的 economical。

normal.en: A car can be economical because it manages fuel like a careful manager.
normal.cn: 一辆车可以很 economical，因为它像谨慎的管家那样管理燃料。

normal.en: Economical prose wastes neither words nor the reader's time.
normal.cn: 简洁的文风既不浪费字，也不浪费读者的时间。

normal.en: Economical with the truth is a polite way of saying not fully honest.
normal.cn: economical with the truth 是「不完全说实话」的委婉说法。

abstract.en: Picture a tap fitted with a small brass limiter, letting through only what is needed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水龙头装了小小的黄铜限流器，只放行必需的量。

abstract.en: The same limiting can apply to fuel, money, words or a machine's appetite.
abstract.cn: 同一种「限量」可以用在燃料、金钱、字句，或一台机器的胃口上。

abstract.en: Economical means the flow is cut to exactly what the job requires.
abstract.cn: economical 意味着流量被削减到正好够用。

examples.en: This small car is economical to run.
examples.cn: 这辆小车用起来很省钱。

examples.en: The household is economical with water in dry summers.
examples.cn: 干旱的夏天里，这家人很节约用水。

examples.en: Her economical prose leaves no sentence to cut.
examples.cn: 她的文风简洁，没有一句是可以删的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊科诺米扣」——低瓦数灯泡配限流器，一滴不浪费

root: 希腊语 oikonomikos「擅长家务管理」经拉丁语 oeconomicus 进入英语；与 economic 同源，但 economical 专指节约、低耗与简洁。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of economical all cut waste: money and resources, fuel and running costs, and words.
sensesIntro.cn: economical 的三个义项都在削减浪费：钱财与资源、燃料与运行成本，以及字句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tap is fitted with a small brass limiter that passes only what is needed.
core.cn: 核心意象：水龙头装了小小的黄铜限流器，只放行必需的量。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: money and resources used without waste.
branches.cn: 家户线：不浪费地使用钱财与资源。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: low fuel and low cost in operation.
branches.cn: 机器线：运行时燃料少、成本低。

branches.en: THE PROSE: words cut to exactly what the meaning needs.
branches.cn: 文句线：字句被削减到正好承载意思。

branches.en: THE BUDGET: a person and a machine both spend little to do the job.
branches.cn: 预算线：人与机器都花很少就完成了任务。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY OF MEANS: thrift applied to money and to language alike.
branches.cn: 手段经济线：节俭同样用于金钱与语言。

intro.en: Economical is a Greek-derived adjective with Latin and French passage, plus ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: economical 是源自希腊语的形容词，经拉丁语与法语过渡，再加普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin oeconomicus is recorded as the intermediate adjective between Greek and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oeconomicus 是希腊语与英语之间有记录的中间形容词。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the source of the sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是词义来源。

items.example: Latin carried the adjective into learned use.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词带入书面语。

items.meaning: to make or act in a way

definition_zh: 宽度；广度；气度
definition_en: the distance from one side of something to the other
core_image: 双臂展开量出的宽度
scene: 他张开双臂量桌面的宽度。 He spread his arms to measure the breadth of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 breadth 是「宽度」（第 1 个义项：从一侧到另一侧的距离）；句意是他张开双臂量桌面的宽度。

senses.title: Distance across
senses.definition: the distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧到另一侧的距离
senses.example: He spread his arms to measure the breadth of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他张开双臂量桌面的宽度。
senses.why: This is the physical sense, from broad plus -th.
senses.whyCN: 这是实体义，由 broad 加 -th 构成。

senses.title: Range of knowledge
senses.definition: the wide range that something covers
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所覆盖的宽广范围
senses.example: The breadth of her reading impressed us.
senses.exampleCN: 她阅读的广度让我们印象深刻。
senses.why: Width became a picture for the range of a subject.
senses.whyCN: 宽度被用来比喻一个主题的范围。

senses.title: Openness of mind
senses.definition: the quality of accepting many different ideas
senses.definitionCN: 能接纳许多不同想法的品质
senses.example: He answered with unexpected breadth.
senses.exampleCN: 他以出人意料的气度作答。
senses.why: A wide space suggested a wide and open mind.
senses.whyCN: 宽广的空间让人联想到开阔的心胸。

intro.en: Breadth was formed in English from broad plus the suffix -th.
intro.cn: breadth 由 broad 加后缀 -th 在英语内部构成。

items.en: brad named a wide thing.
items.cn: brad 指宽大的事物。

items.en: breadthe named the distance across.
items.cn: breadthe 指横向的距离。

items.en: breadth also meant wide knowledge.
items.cn: breadth 也指广博的知识。

items.en: breadth described an open mind.
items.cn: breadth 形容开阔的心胸。

items.en: breadth covers width, range and openness.
items.cn: 如今 breadth 兼指宽度、范围与气度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -eadth or br- shape; the near-meaning group gives other measures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -eadth 或 br- 的外形；近义组是其他度量词。

normalIntro.en: Breadth is the wide measure that broad turns into a noun.
normalIntro.cn: breadth 是 broad 变来的名词，表示宽的量。

normal.en: Measure the breadth of the table.
normal.cn: 量一量桌面的宽度。

normal.en: The breadth of her reading is great.
normal.cn: 她阅读的广度很大。

normal.en: Length and breadth both matter.
normal.cn: 长与宽都要紧。

normal.en: The noun ends in -th.
normal.cn: 这个名词以 -th 结尾。

normal.en: He has breadth of mind.
normal.cn: 他心胸开阔。

abstract.en: See two arms stretched wide.
abstract.cn: 想象两条手臂张得很开。

abstract.en: See a shelf of books on many subjects.
abstract.cn: 想象一书架各科的书。

abstract.en: See an open door letting in many views.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇敞开的门放进许多风景。
